documents.text: Even though the face-up plane or phenomenon is controlled by just one player, any ability of that plane or phenomenon that refers to “you” applies to both members of the planar controller’s team.

documents.title: 901.12d — Planechase
documents.text: Since each member of the active team is an active player, each of them may roll the planar die. Each player’s cost to roll the planar die is based on the number of times that particular player has already rolled the planar die that turn.

documents.title: 901.13 — Planechase
documents.text: In multiplayer formats other than Grand Melee, plane cards and phenomenon cards are exempt from the limited range of influence option. Their abilities, and the effects of those abilities, affect all applicable objects and players in the game. (See rule 801, “Limited Range of Influence Option.”)

documents.title: 901.14 — Planechase
documents.text: In Grand Melee Planechase games, multiple plane cards or phenomenon cards may be face up at the same time.

documents.title: 901.14a — Planechase
documents.text: Before the first turn of the game of the game, each player who will start the game with a turn marker sets a starting plane (see rule 901.5). Each of them is a planar controller.

documents.title: 901.14b — Planechase
documents.text: If a player would leave the game and that player leaving the game would reduce the number of turn markers in the game, that player first ceases to be a planar controller (but no other player becomes a planar controller), then that player leaves the game. Each face-up plane card or phenomenon card that player controlled is put on the bottom of its owner’s planar deck. No player is considered to have planeswalked.

documents.title: 901.15 — Single Planar Deck Option
documents.text: Single Planar Deck Option

documents.title: 901.15a — Single Planar Deck Option
documents.text: As an alternative option, a Planechase game may be played with just a single communal planar deck. In that case, the number of cards in the planar deck must be at least forty or at least ten times the number of players in the game, whichever is smaller. The planar deck can’t contain more phenomenon cards than twice the number of players in the game. Each card in the planar deck must have a different English name.

documents.title: 901.15b — Single Planar Deck Option
documents.text: In a Planechase game using the single planar deck option, the planar controller is considered to be the owner of all cards in the planar deck.

documents.title: 901.15c — Single Planar Deck Option
documents.text: If any rule or ability refers to a player’s planar deck, the communal planar deck is used.

documents.title: Vanguard
documents.text: Vanguard

documents.title: 902.1 — Vanguard
documents.text: In the Vanguard variant, a vanguard card allows each player to play the role of a famous character. Each player will have one face-up vanguard card whose abilities and other characteristics affect the game. The Vanguard variant uses all the normal rules for a Magic game, with the following additions.

documents.title: 902.2 — Vanguard
documents.text: A Vanguard game may be a two-player game or a multiplayer game.

documents.title: 902.3 — Vanguard
documents.text: In addition to the normal game materials, each player needs a vanguard card. Each vanguard card is placed face up next to its owner’s library before the game begins. All vanguard cards remain in the command zone throughout the game.

documents.title: 902.4 — Vanguard
documents.text:
Each player’s starting life total is 20 plus or minus the life modifier of their vanguard card.
Example: The life modifier of a player’s vanguard card is -3. That player’s starting life total is 17.

documents.title: 902.5 — Vanguard
documents.text: Each player’s starting hand size is seven cards, as modified by the hand modifier of their vanguard card.

documents.title: 902.5a — Vanguard
documents.text:
If a player takes a mulligan in a Vanguard game, just like in a normal game, that player shuffles their hand back into their library, then draws a new hand equal to their starting hand size. (In a multiplayer game, a player’s first mulligan is for the same number of cards as they had before.) See rule 103.5.
Example: The hand modifier of a player’s vanguard card is +2. That player starts the game with a hand of 9 cards. If the player takes a mulligan three times before keeping, they draw a new hand of nine cards and put three of those on the bottom of their library.

documents.title: 902.5b — Vanguard
documents.text:
A player’s maximum hand size is seven, as modified by the hand modifier of their vanguard card.
Example: The hand modifier of a player’s vanguard card is -1. That player’s maximum hand size is six. If that player has more than six cards in their hand as their cleanup step begins, they will discard all but six of them.

documents.title: 902.6 — Vanguard
documents.text: The owner of a vanguard card is the player who started the game with it in the command zone. The controller of a face-up vanguard card is its owner.

documents.title: 902.7 — Vanguard
documents.text: Any abilities of a face-up vanguard card in the command zone function from that zone. The card’s static abilities affect the game, its triggered abilities may trigger, and its activated abilities may be activated.

documents.title: Commander
documents.text: Commander

documents.title: 903.1 — Commander
documents.text: In the Commander variant, a variant created and popularized by fans, each deck is led by a legendary creature designated as that deck’s commander. The Commander variant uses all the normal rules for a Magic game, with the following additions.

documents.title: 903.2 — Commander
documents.text: A Commander game may be a two-player game or a multiplayer game. The default multiplayer setup is the Free-for-All variant with the attack multiple players option and without the limited range of influence option. See rule 806, “Free-for-All Variant.”

documents.title: 903.3 — Commander
documents.text:
Each deck has a legendary card designated as its commander. That card must be either (a) a creature card, (b) a Vehicle card, or (c) a Spacecraft card with one or more power/toughness boxes. This designation is not a characteristic of the object represented by the card; rather, it is an attribute of the card itself. The card retains this designation even when it changes zones.
Example: A commander that’s been turned face down (due to Ixidron’s effect, for example) is still a commander. A commander that’s copying another card (due to Cytoshape’s effect, for example) is still a commander. A permanent that’s copying a commander (such as a Body Double, for example, copying a commander in a player’s graveyard) is not a commander.

documents.title: 903.3a — Commander
documents.text: Some cards have an ability that states the card can be your commander. This ability modifies the rules for deck construction, and it functions before the game begins. See also rule 113.6n.

documents.title: 903.3b — Commander
documents.text: If a player’s commander is a meld card and it’s melded with the other member of its meld pair, the resulting melded permanent is that player’s commander.

documents.title: 903.3c — Commander
documents.text: If a player’s commander is a component of a merged permanent, the resulting merged permanent is that player’s commander.

documents.title: 903.3d — Commander
documents.text: If an effect refers to controlling a commander, it refers to a permanent on the battlefield that is a commander. If an effect refers to casting a commander, it refers to a spell that is a commander. If an effect refers to a commander in a specific zone, it refers to a card in that zone that is a commander.

documents.title: 903.3e — Commander
documents.text: If an effect refers to a characteristic of “your commander,” it can find the appropriate player’s commander and see its current characteristics, as modified by continuous effects and other rules, in all zones, including that player’s library and hand.

documents.title: 903.4 — Commander
documents.text:
The Commander variant uses color identity to determine what cards can be in a deck with a certain commander. The color identity of a card is the color or colors of any mana symbols in that card’s mana cost or rules text, plus any colors defined by its characteristic-defining abilities (see rule 604.3) or color indicator (see rule 204).
Example: Bosh, Iron Golem is a legendary artifact creature with mana cost {8} and the ability “{3}{R}, Sacrifice an artifact: Bosh, Iron Golem deals damage equal to the sacrificed artifact’s mana value to any target.” Bosh’s color identity is red.

documents.title: 903.4a — Commander
documents.text: Color identity is established before the game begins. If a rule or effect refers to the color identity of an object in the game represented by a card, it uses the color identity established for that card as the game began.

documents.title: 903.4b — Commander
documents.text: If a commander has a static ability that causes a player to choose its color before the game begins, that choice applies during deck construction and throughout the game, even as the commander changes zones. That choice affects the commander’s color identity. The player reveals that choice as they put their commander into the command zone before the game begins. See rules 103.2c and 607.2p.

documents.title: 903.4c — Commander
documents.text: Reminder text is ignored when determining a card’s color identity. See rule 207.2.

documents.title: 903.4d — Commander
documents.text:
The back face of a double-faced card (see rule 712) is included when determining a card’s color identity. This is an exception to rule 712.8a.
Example: Civilized Scholar is the front face of a double-faced card with mana cost {2}{U}. Homicidal Brute is the back face of that double-faced card and has a red color indicator. The card’s color identity is blue and red.

documents.title: 903.4e — Commander
documents.text: If a card has any alternative characteristics, such as those of adventurer cards (see rule 715, “Adventurer Cards”), those characteristics are included when determining the card’s color identity.

documents.title: 903.4f — Commander
documents.text: If an ability refers to the colors or number of colors in a commander’s color identity, that quality is undefined if that player doesn’t have a commander. That part of the ability won’t do anything. Costs that refer to that quality are unpayable.

documents.title: 903.5 — Commander
documents.text: Each Commander deck is subject to the following deck construction rules.

documents.title: 903.5a — Commander
documents.text: Each deck must contain exactly 100 cards, including its commander. In other words, the minimum deck size and the maximum deck size are both 100.

documents.title: 903.5b — Commander
documents.text: Other than basic lands, each card in a Commander deck must have a different English name. For the purposes of deck construction, cards with interchangeable names have the same English name (see rule 201.3).

documents.title: 903.5c — Commander
documents.text:
A card can be included in a Commander deck only if every color in its color identity is also found in the color identity of the deck’s commander.
Example: Wort, the Raidmother is a legendary creature with mana cost {4}{R/G}{R/G}. Wort’s color identity is red and green. Each card in a Wort Commander deck must be only red, only green, both red and green, or have no color. Each mana symbol in the mana cost or rules text of a card in this deck must be only red, only green, both red and green, or have no color.

documents.title: 903.5d — Commander
documents.text:
A card with a basic land type may be included in a Commander deck only if each color of mana it could produce is included in the commander’s color identity.
Example: Wort, the Raidmother’s color identity is red and green. A Wort Commander deck may include land cards with the basic land types Mountain and/or Forest. It can’t include any land cards with the basic land types Plains, Island, or Swamp.

documents.title: 903.5e — Commander
documents.text: Commander games do not use sideboards.

documents.title: 903.6 — Commander
documents.text: At the start of the game, each player puts their commander from their deck face up into the command zone. Then each player shuffles the remaining cards of their deck so that the cards are in a random order. Those cards become the player’s library.

documents.title: 903.7 — Commander
documents.text: Once the starting player has been determined, each player sets their life total to 40 and draws a hand of seven cards.

documents.title: 903.8 — Commander
documents.text: A player may cast a commander they own from the command zone. A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game. This additional cost is informally known as the “commander tax.”

documents.title: 903.9 — Commander
documents.text: A commander may return to the command zone during a Commander game.

documents.title: 903.9a — Commander
documents.text: If a commander is in a graveyard or in exile and that object was put into that zone since the last time state-based actions were checked, its owner may put it into the command zone. This is a state-based action. See rule 704.

documents.title: 903.9b — Commander
documents.text: If a commander would be put into its owner’s hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead. This replacement effect may apply more than once to the same event. This is an exception to rule 614.5.

documents.title: 903.9c — Commander
documents.text: If a commander is a melded permanent or a merged permanent and its owner chooses to put it into the command zone using the replacement effect described in rule 903.9b, that permanent and each component representing it that isn’t a commander are put into the appropriate zone, and the card that represents it and is a commander is put into the command zone.

documents.title: 903.10 — Commander
documents.text: The Commander variant includes the following specification for winning and losing the game. All other rules for ending the game also apply. (See rule 104.)

documents.title: 903.10a — Commander
documents.text: A player who’s been dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander over the course of the game loses the game. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

documents.title: 903.11 — Commander
documents.text: Except via rules, special actions, and effects that specifically bring cards into Commander games from outside the game, traditional cards from outside the game cannot be brought into a Commander game.

documents.title: 903.11a — Commander
documents.text: If a player is allowed to bring a card from outside the game into a Commander game, that player can’t bring a card into the game this way if it has the same name as a card that player had in their starting deck, if it has the same name as a card that the player owns in the current game, or if any color in its color identity isn’t in the color identity of the player’s commander.

documents.title: 903.12 — Brawl Option
documents.text: Brawl Option

documents.title: 903.12a — Brawl Option
documents.text: Brawl is an option for a different style of Commander game. Brawl games use the normal rules for the Commander variant with the following modifications.

documents.title: 903.12b — Brawl Option
documents.text: Brawl decks are usually constructed using cards from the Standard format.

documents.title: 903.12c — Brawl Option
documents.text: Each deck has a legendary card designated as its commander. That card must be either (a) a creature card, (b) a planeswalker card, (c) a Vehicle card, or (d) a Spacecraft card with one or more power/toughness boxes.

documents.title: 903.12d — Brawl Option
documents.text: A player’s deck must contain exactly 60 cards, including its commander. In other words, the minimum deck size and the maximum deck size are both 60.

documents.title: 903.12e — Brawl Option
documents.text: If a player’s commander has no colors in its color identity, that player’s deck may contain any number of basic lands of one basic land type of their choice. This is an exception to rule 903.5d.

documents.title: 903.12f — Brawl Option
documents.text: In a two-player Brawl game, each player’s starting life total is 25. In a multiplayer Brawl game, each player’s starting life total is 30.

documents.title: 903.12g — Brawl Option
documents.text: In any Brawl game, the first mulligan a player takes doesn’t count toward the number of cards that player will put on the bottom of their library or the number of mulligans that player may take. Subsequent mulligans are counted toward these numbers as normal.

documents.title: 903.12h — Brawl Option
documents.text: Brawl games do not use the state-based action described in rule 704.6c, which causes a player to lose the game if they’ve been dealt 21 or more combat damage by a commander.

documents.title: 903.13 — Commander Draft
documents.text: Commander Draft

documents.title: 903.13a — Commander Draft
documents.text: Commander Draft is an option for a different style of Commander game. It consists of a draft (a style of limited play where players choose cards from sealed booster packs to build their decks) followed by a multiplayer game. The Commander Draft option uses Commander Legends booster packs by default.

documents.title: 903.13b — Commander Draft
documents.text: A draft typically consists of three draft rounds. In each draft round, each player opens a booster pack, drafts two cards by placing them in a face-down pile in front of them, then passes the remaining cards to the next player. Each player then drafts two cards from the booster pack passed to them and passes the remaining cards. This procedure continues until all cards in that draft round have been drafted.

documents.title: 903.13c — Commander Draft
documents.text: In the first and third draft rounds, booster packs are passed to each player’s left. In the second draft round, booster packs are passed to each player’s right.

documents.title: 903.13d — Commander Draft
documents.text: During the draft, a player can look only at cards in the booster pack they are currently drafting from and cards they have already drafted. A player may not reveal drafted cards to other players unless an ability instructs them to.

documents.title: 903.13e — Commander Draft
documents.text: After the draft is complete, the cards a player drafted become that player’s card pool. If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Legends or Commander Masters, each player may add up to two cards named The Prismatic Piper to their card pool, but only if those cards are used as the player’s commander(s). If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur’s Gate®, each player may add up to two cards named Faceless One to their card pool, but only if those cards are used as the player’s commander(s).

documents.title: 903.13f — Commander Draft
documents.text: Commander Draft deck construction follows the same rules as Commander deck construction (see rule 903.5) with three exceptions: (1) A player’s deck must contain at least 60 cards. There is no maximum deck size. (2) A player’s deck may include any number of cards from that player’s card pool with the same name. (3) If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Masters, any card which can be a player’s commander by itself and whose color identity includes one or fewer colors is considered to have the partner ability for the purposes of deckbuilding. (See rule 702.124, “Partner.”)

documents.title: 903.13g — Commander Draft
documents.text: Commander Draft games follow the same rules as Commander games. See rules 903.6–903.11.

documents.title: Archenemy
documents.text: Archenemy

documents.title: 904.1 — Archenemy
documents.text: In the Archenemy variant, a team of players faces off against a single opponent strengthened with powerful scheme cards. The Archenemy variant uses all the normal rules for a Magic game, with the following additions.

documents.title: 904.2 — Archenemy
documents.text: The default setup for an Archenemy game is the Team vs. Team multiplayer variant (see rule 808) involving exactly two teams. The attack multiple players option (see rule 802) and the shared team turns option (see rule 805) are used; no other multiplayer options are used.

documents.title: 904.2a — Archenemy
documents.text: One of the teams consists of exactly one player, who is designated the archenemy.

documents.title: 904.2b — Archenemy
documents.text: The other team consists of any number of players.

documents.title: 904.3 — Archenemy
documents.text: In addition to the normal game materials, the archenemy needs a supplementary scheme deck of at least twenty scheme cards. A scheme deck may contain no more than two of any card with a particular English name. (See rule 314, “Schemes.”)

documents.title: 904.4 — Archenemy
documents.text: All scheme cards remain in the command zone throughout the game, both while they’re part of a scheme deck and while they’re face up.

documents.title: 904.5 — Archenemy
documents.text: The archenemy’s starting life total is 40. Each other player’s starting life total is 20.

documents.title: 904.6 — Archenemy
documents.text: Rather than a randomly determined player, the archenemy takes the first turn of the game.

documents.title: 904.7 — Archenemy
documents.text: The owner of a scheme card is the player who started the game with it in the command zone. The controller of a face-up scheme card is its owner.

documents.title: 904.8 — Archenemy
documents.text: Any abilities of a face-up scheme card in the command zone function from that zone. The card’s static abilities affect the game, its triggered abilities may trigger, and its activated abilities may be activated.

documents.title: 904.9 — Archenemy
documents.text: Immediately after the archenemy’s precombat main phase begins during each of their turns, that player moves the top card of their scheme deck off that scheme deck and turns it face up. This is called “setting that scheme in motion.” (See rule 701.32.) This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. Abilities of that scheme card that trigger “When you set this scheme in motion” trigger.

documents.title: 904.10 — Archenemy
documents.text: If a non-ongoing scheme card is face up in the command zone, and no triggered abilities of any scheme are on the stack or waiting to be put on the stack, that scheme card is turned face down and put on the bottom of its owner’s scheme deck the next time a player would receive priority. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

documents.title: 904.11 — Archenemy
documents.text: Once an ongoing scheme card is set in motion, it remains face up in the command zone until an ability causes it to be abandoned (see rule 701.33).

documents.title: 904.12 — Supervillain Rumble Option
documents.text: Supervillain Rumble Option

documents.title: 904.12a — Supervillain Rumble Option
documents.text: As an alternative option, players may play a Free-for-All game in which each player has their own scheme deck. The attack multiple players option (see rule 802) is used; no other multiplayer options are used.

documents.title: 904.12b — Supervillain Rumble Option
documents.text: Each player in this game is an archenemy.

documents.title: 904.12c — Supervillain Rumble Option
documents.text: As in a normal Free-for-All game, the starting player is randomly determined. All other rules that apply to the archenemy in an Archenemy game apply to each player in a Supervillain Rumble game.

documents.title: 904.13 — Archenemy Commander Option
documents.text: Archenemy Commander Option

documents.title: 904.13a — Archenemy Commander Option
documents.text: As an alternative option, players may play a Commander game (see rule 903, “Commander”) using the Archenemy rules. The normal rules for Commander apply, as modified by the Archenemy rules, with the following exceptions.

documents.title: 904.13b — Archenemy Commander Option
documents.text: The archenemy starts with 60 life. The opposing team has a shared life total that starts at 60 life rather than individual life totals. The use of a shared life total is detailed in rules 810.8 and 810.9 of the Two-Headed Giant variant.

documents.title: 904.13c — Archenemy Commander Option
documents.text: Poison counters are not shared. If the archenemy has ten or more poison counters, they lose the game. If any individual member of the opposing team has ten or more poison counters, they lose the game. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

documents.title: 904.13d — Archenemy Commander Option
documents.text: The archenemy’s scheme deck must contain at least ten cards, and each card must have a different English name.

documents.title: Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Conspiracy Draft

documents.title: 905.1 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: The Conspiracy Draft variant consists of a draft (a style of limited play where players choose cards from sealed booster packs to build their decks) followed by a multiplayer game. The Conspiracy Draft variant uses Magic: The Gathering—Conspiracy® and/or Conspiracy: Take the Crown booster packs by default.

documents.title: 905.1a — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: A draft typically consists of three draft rounds. In each draft round, each player opens a booster pack, drafts one card by placing that card in a face-down pile in front of the player, then passes the remaining cards to the next player. Each player then drafts a card from the booster pack passed to them and passes the remaining cards. This procedure continues until all cards in that draft round have been drafted.

documents.title: 905.1b — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: In the first and third draft rounds, booster packs are passed to each player’s left. In the second draft round, booster packs are passed to each player’s right.

documents.title: 905.1c — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: During the draft, a player can look only at cards in the booster pack they are currently drafting from, cards they have already drafted, cards that are currently revealed as described in rule 905.2b, and cards that have been drafted face up as described in rule 905.2c. A player may not reveal drafted cards to other players unless an ability instructs them to.

documents.title: 905.1d — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: After the draft and all actions that may be taken during or after the draft, all the cards a player has drafted become that player’s card pool. The player builds their deck from only these cards and any number of basic land cards. See rules 100.2b and 100.4b.

documents.title: 905.2 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Some cards have abilities that function during the draft.

documents.title: 905.2a — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: During a draft, there is no active player or system of priority. If multiple players wish to take an action at the same time during the draft and can’t agree on an order, those actions are taken in a random order.

documents.title: 905.2b — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Some cards instruct players to reveal them as they’re drafted and then note some information, such as a number or color. This information can be referred to by other abilities during the game. Any player can look at this information at any time during the draft or game. After the information is noted, the drafted card is turned face down and added to the player’s drafted cards pile.

documents.title: 905.2c — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Some cards instruct players to draft them face up. Each such card remains face up until the draft is complete, an effect instructs the player who drafted it to turn it face down, or the card leaves that player’s drafted cards pile. While the card is face up, all players may look at it.

documents.title: 905.3 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: A Conspiracy Draft game is a multiplayer game. The default multiplayer setup is the Free-for-All variant with the attack multiple players option and without the limited range of influence option. See rule 806, “Free-for-All Variant.”

documents.title: 905.4 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: At the start of the game, before decks are shuffled, each player may put any number of conspiracy cards from their sideboard into the command zone.

documents.title: 905.4a — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Conspiracy cards with hidden agenda are put into the command zone face down. Any time a player has priority, they may turn a face-down conspiracy card they control face up. See rule 702.106, “Hidden Agenda.”

documents.title: 905.5 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: The owner of a conspiracy card is the player who put it into the command zone at the start of the game. The controller of a conspiracy card is its owner.

documents.title: 905.6 — Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: Once the starting player has been determined, each player sets their life total to 20 and draws a hand of seven cards.

documents.title: Abandon
documents.text: To turn a face-up ongoing scheme card face down and put it on the bottom of its owner’s scheme deck. See rule 701.33, “Abandon.”

documents.title: Ability
documents.text:
1. Text on an object that explains what that object does or can do.
2. An activated or triggered ability on the stack. This kind of ability is an object.
See rule 113, “Abilities,” and section 6, “Spells, Abilities, and Effects.”

documents.title: Ability Word
documents.text: An italicized word with no rules meaning that ties together abilities on different cards that have similar functionality. See rule 207.2c.

documents.title: Absorb
documents.text: A keyword ability that prevents damage. See rule 702.64, “Absorb.”

documents.title: Activate
documents.text: To put an activated ability onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its effect. See rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

documents.title: Activated Ability
documents.text: A kind of ability. Activated abilities are written as “[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]” See rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

documents.title: Activation Cost
documents.text: Everything that appears before the colon in an activated ability’s text. It must be paid to activate the ability. See rule 118, “Costs,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

documents.title: Active Player
documents.text: The player whose turn it is. See rule 102.1.

documents.title: Active Player, Nonactive Player Order
documents.text: A system that determines the order by which players make choices if multiple players are instructed to make choices at the same time. See rule 101.4. This rule is modified for games using the shared team turns option; see rule 805.6.

documents.title: Active Team
documents.text: The team whose turn it is in a game using the shared team turns option. See rule 805.4a.

documents.title: Adapt
documents.text: A keyword action that puts +1/+1 counters on a creature that doesn’t have any yet. See rule 701.46, “Adapt.”

documents.title: Additional Cost
documents.text: A cost a spell may have that its controller may pay (or, in some cases, must pay) in addition to its mana cost to cast that spell. See rule 118, “Costs,” and rule 601, “Casting Spells.”

documents.title: Adventurer Card
documents.text: Cards with a two-part card frame (one part of which is inset on the left) on a single card where the alternative characteristics include the Adventure spell type. See rule 715, “Adventurer Cards.”

documents.title: Affinity
documents.text: A keyword ability that reduces how much mana you need to spend to cast a spell. See rule 702.41, “Affinity.”

documents.title: Afflict
documents.text: A keyword ability that makes the defending player lose life for blocking. See rule 702.130, “Afflict.”

documents.title: Afterlife
documents.text: A keyword ability that leaves behind Spirit creature tokens when certain creatures die. See rule 702.135, “Afterlife.”

documents.title: Aftermath
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast one half of a split card only from their graveyard. See rule 702.127, “Aftermath.”

documents.title: Airbend
documents.text: A keyword action that exiles one or more permanents and/or spells. The owner of each card exiled with airbend may cast it from exile by paying {2} rather than paying its mana cost. See rule 701.65, “Airbend.”

documents.title: Alternate Name
documents.text: A different name used on promotional or alternate-art versions of some cards. This name has no rules meaning. See rule 201.6.

documents.title: Alternating Teams Variant
documents.text: A multiplayer variant played among two or more teams of equal size. See rule 811, “Alternating Teams Variant.”

documents.title: Alternative Cost
documents.text: A cost a spell may have that its controller can pay rather than paying its mana cost. See rule 118, “Costs,” and rule 601, “Casting Spells.”

documents.title: Amass
documents.text: A keyword action that gives you a Zombie Army creature token or grows an Army you already have. See rule 701.47, “Amass.”

documents.title: Amplify
documents.text: A keyword ability than can have a creature enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 702.38, “Amplify.”

documents.title: Anchor Word
documents.text: A word that precedes one of two abilities a permanent may enter the battlefield with. See rule 614.12b.

documents.title: Annihilator
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature particularly brutal when it attacks. See rule 702.86, “Annihilator.”

documents.title: Ante
documents.text:
1. A zone used only when playing “for keeps.”
2. To put a card into the ante zone.
See rule 407, “Ante.”

documents.title: Any Target
documents.text: A spell or ability may require “any target.” “Any target” is the same as “target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle.” See rule 115.4.

documents.title: APNAP Order
documents.text: See Active Player, Nonactive Player Order.

documents.title: Archenemy
documents.text:
1. A casual variant in which a team of players faces off against a single opponent strengthened with powerful scheme cards. See rule 904, “Archenemy.”
2. A player in an Archenemy game who is playing with a scheme deck.

documents.title: Archenemy Commander
documents.text: A Commander game that follows a modified version of the Archenemy rules. See rule 903, “Commander,” and rule 904, “Archenemy.”

documents.title: Artifact
documents.text: A card type. An artifact is a permanent. See rule 301, “Artifacts.”

documents.title: Artifact Creature
documents.text: A combination of artifact and creature that’s subject to the rules for both. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 302, “Creatures.”

documents.title: Artifact Land
documents.text: A combination of artifact and land that’s subject to the rules for both. Artifact lands can only be played as lands, not cast as spells. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 305, “Lands.”

documents.title: Artifact Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the artifact card type. See rule 301, “Artifacts.” See rule 205.3g for the list of artifact types.

documents.title: As Though
documents.text: Text used to indicate that the game, for some specific purpose, treats a condition as true even though it’s not. See rule 609.4.

documents.title: Ascend
documents.text: A keyword causing a player to get the designation of the city’s blessing once they control ten permanents. See rule 702.131, “Ascend.”

documents.title: Assemble
documents.text: Assemble is a keyword action in the Unstable set that puts Contraptions onto the battlefield. Cards and mechanics from the Unstable set aren’t included in these rules.

documents.title: Assign Combat Damage
documents.text: To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

documents.title: Assist
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets another player help you pay for a spell. See rule 702.132, “Assist.”

documents.title: At End of Turn (Obsolete)
documents.text: A trigger condition printed on abilities that triggered at the beginning of the end step (which is not the last thing to happen in the turn). Cards that were printed with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to say “at the beginning of the end step” or “at the beginning of the next end step.” See rule 513, “End Step.”

documents.title: Attach
documents.text: To take an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification from where it currently is and put it onto a specified object or player. See rule 701.3, “Attach.”

documents.title: Attack
documents.text: To send a creature into combat offensively. A creature can attack a player or a planeswalker. See rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

documents.title: Attack Alone
documents.text: A creature “attacks alone” if it’s the only creature declared as an attacker during the declare attackers step. A creature “is attacking alone” if it’s attacking but no other creatures are. See rule 506.5.

documents.title: Attack Left Option
documents.text: An option that may be used in certain multiplayer variants. See rule 803, “Attack Left and Attack Right Options.”

documents.title: Attack Multiple Players Option
documents.text: An option that may be used in certain multiplayer variants. See rule 802, “Attack Multiple Players Option.”

documents.title: Attack Right Option
documents.text: An option that may be used in certain multiplayer variants. See rule 803, “Attack Left and Attack Right Options.”

documents.title: Attacking Creature
documents.text: A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal attack during the combat phase (once all costs to attack, if any, have been paid), or a creature that has been put onto the battlefield attacking. It remains an attacking creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

documents.title: Attacking Team
documents.text: The team who can attack during the combat phase of a multiplayer game using the shared team turns option. See rule 805, “Shared Team Turns Option.”

documents.title: Attacks and Isn’t Blocked
documents.text: An ability that triggers when a creature “attacks and isn’t blocked” triggers when the creature becomes an unblocked attacking creature. See rule 509.1h.

documents.title: Attraction
documents.text: An artifact type seen only on nontraditional Magic cards in the Unfinity expansion. See rule 717, “Attraction Cards,” rule 701.51, “Open an Attraction,” and rule 701.52, “Roll to Visit Your Attractions.”

documents.title: Attraction Deck
documents.text: An optional deck of at least three (in limited play) or ten (in constructed play) Attraction cards that can be used to support play with some cards from the Unfinity expansion. See rule 717.2.

documents.title: Aura
documents.text: An enchantment subtype. Aura spells target objects or players, and Aura permanents are attached to objects or players. See rule 303, “Enchantments,” and rule 702.5, “Enchant.”

documents.title: Aura Swap
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you exchange an Aura on the battlefield with one in your hand. See rule 702.65, “Aura Swap.”

documents.title: Awaken
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you turn a land you control into a creature. See rule 702.113, “Awaken.”

documents.title: Background
documents.text: An enchantment type that, in combination with the “choose a Background” ability, may allow a legendary enchantment card to be your commander. See rule 702.124, “Partner,” and rule 903, “Commander.”

documents.title: Backup
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature give +1/+1 counters to itself or another when it enters the battlefield. If a different creature is chosen, that creature also temporarily gains one or more abilities. See rule 702.165, “Backup.”

documents.title: Banding, “Bands with Other”
documents.text: Banding is a keyword ability that modifies the rules for declaring attackers and assigning combat damage. “Bands with other” is a specialized version of the ability. See rule 702.22, “Banding.”

documents.title: Bargain
documents.text: Bargain is a keyword ability that represents an optional additional cost of sacrificing an artifact, enchantment, or token. A spell has been bargained if its controller declared the intention to pay that cost. See rule 702.166, “Bargain.”

documents.title: Base Power, Base Toughness
documents.text: Effects that change the base power and/or base toughness of a creature set one or both of those values to a specific number. See rule 613, “Interaction of Continuous Effects.”

documents.title: Basic
documents.text: A supertype that’s normally relevant on lands. Any land with this supertype is a basic land. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.”

documents.title: Basic Land Type
documents.text: There are five “basic land types”: Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. Each one has a mana ability associated with it. See rule 305, “Lands.”

documents.title: Basic Landcycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Battle
documents.text: A card type. A battle is a permanent. See rule 310, “Battles.”

documents.title: Battle Cry
documents.text: A keyword ability that makes other attacking creatures better in combat. See rule 702.91, “Battle Cry.”

documents.title: Battlefield
documents.text: A zone. The battlefield is the zone in which permanents exist. It used to be known as the “in-play” zone. See rule 403, “Battlefield.”

documents.title: Becomes
documents.text: A word used in some trigger events to indicate a change in status or characteristics. See rule 603.2e.

documents.title: Beginning of Combat Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the combat phase. See rule 507, “Beginning of Combat Step.”

documents.title: Beginning Phase
documents.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the first phase of the turn. See rule 501, “Beginning Phase.”

documents.title: Behold
documents.text: A keyword action that allows a player to choose a permanent they control of a particular quality or reveal a card of that quality from their hand, usually to pay a cost or get an additional effect. See rule 701.4, “Behold.”

documents.title: Bestow
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature card be cast as an Aura. See rule 702.103, “Bestow.”

documents.title: Blight
documents.text: A keyword action. To blight N means to put N -1/-1 counters on a creature you control. See rule 701.68, “Blight.”

documents.title: Blitz
documents.text: A keyword ability found on creature cards that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule 702.152, “Blitz.”

documents.title: Block
documents.text: To send a creature into combat defensively. A creature can block an attacking creature. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

documents.title: Block Alone
documents.text: A creature “blocks alone” if it’s the only creature declared as a blocker during the declare blockers step. A creature “is blocking alone” if it’s blocking but no other creatures are. See rule 506.5.

documents.title: Blocked Creature
documents.text: An attacking creature that another creature blocks or that an effect causes to become blocked. It remains a blocked creature until it’s removed from combat, an effect says that it becomes unblocked, or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

documents.title: Blocking Creature
documents.text: A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal block during the combat phase (once all costs to block, if any, have been paid), or a creature that has been put onto the battlefield blocking. It remains a blocking creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

documents.title: Blood Token
documents.text: A Blood token is a colorless artifact token with “{1}, {T}, Discard a card, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Bloodthirst
documents.text: A keyword ability that can have a creature enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 702.54, “Bloodthirst.”

documents.title: Boast
documents.text: An activated ability that can be activated only once each turn if the creature with the boast ability attacked that turn. See rule 702.142, “Boast.”

documents.title: Bolster
documents.text: A keyword action that puts +1/+1 counters on the weakest creature a player controls. See rule 701.39, “Bolster.”

documents.title: Booster Pack
documents.text: A group of unopened Magic cards from a particular expansion. Booster packs are used in Limited formats. See rule 100.2b.

documents.title: Brawl
documents.text: An option for the Commander casual variant. See rule 903.12, “Brawl Option.”

documents.title: Bury (Obsolete)
documents.text: A term that meant “put [a permanent] into its owner’s graveyard.” In general, cards that were printed with the term “bury” have received errata in the Oracle card reference to read, “Destroy [a permanent]. It can’t be regenerated,” or “Sacrifice [a permanent].”

documents.title: Bushido
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature better in combat. See rule 702.45, “Bushido.”

documents.title: Buyback
documents.text: A keyword ability of instants and sorceries that can let the spell return to its owner’s hand as it resolves. See rule 702.27, “Buyback.”

documents.title: Card
documents.text: The standard component of the game. Magic cards may be traditional or nontraditional. Tokens aren’t considered cards. In the text of spells or abilities, the term “card” is used only to refer to a card that’s not on the battlefield or on the stack, such as a creature card in a player’s hand. See rule 108, “Cards.”

documents.title: Card Pool
documents.text: In a Limited format, the cards a player may use, in addition to basic land cards, to build their deck.

documents.title: Card Type
documents.text: A characteristic. Except for abilities on the stack, each object has a card type, even if that object isn’t a card. Each card type has its own rules. See rule 205, “Type Line,” and section 3, “Card Types.”

documents.title: Cascade
documents.text: A keyword ability that may let a player cast a random extra spell for no cost. See rule 702.85, “Cascade.”

documents.title: Case
documents.text: An enchantment subtype. Cases have a “to solve” ability that set a condition its controller must meet in order for the “solved” ability to take effect. See rule 719, “Case Cards.”

documents.title: Cast
documents.text: To take a card from where it is (usually the hand), put it on the stack, and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its effect. See rule 601, “Casting Spells.”

documents.title: Caster (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term that referred to the player who cast a spell. In general, cards that were printed with the term “caster” have received errata in the Oracle card reference to say “controller.”

documents.title: Casting Cost (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for mana cost. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Casualty
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to sacrifice a creature to create a copy of a spell. See 702.153, “Casualty.”

documents.title: Champion, Championed
documents.text: “Champion” is a keyword ability that lets one creature temporarily replace another. A permanent is “championed” by another permanent if the latter exiles the former as the direct result of a champion ability. See rule 702.72, “Champion.”

documents.title: Change a Target
documents.text: To choose a new, legal target for a spell or ability. See rule 115.7.

documents.title: Changeling
documents.text: A characteristic-defining ability that grants the object it’s on every creature type. See rule 702.73, “Changeling.”

documents.title: Chaos Ability
documents.text: An ability of a plane card that triggers “Whenever chaos ensues” in the Planechase casual variant. See rule 311.7.

documents.title: Chaos Symbol
documents.text: The chaos symbol appears on the planar die and near some triggered abilities of plane cards in the Planechase casual variant. See rule 107.12.

documents.title: Characteristic-Defining Ability
documents.text: A kind of static ability that conveys information about an object’s characteristics that would normally be found elsewhere on that object (such as in its mana cost, type line, or power/toughness box). See rule 604.3.

documents.title: Characteristics
documents.text: Information that defines an object. See rule 109.3.

documents.title: Choose a Background
documents.text: A variant of the partner ability that lets two legendary permanent cards be your commander in the Commander variant rather than one if one of them has the “choose a Background” ability and the other is a Background enchantment card. See rule 702.124, “Partner,” and rule 903, “Commander.”

documents.title: Cipher
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to encode a card on a creature and cast that card whenever that creature deals combat damage to a player. See rule 702.99, “Cipher.”

documents.title: City’s Blessing
documents.text: A designation a player can have. The ascend keyword causes a player to get this designation once they control ten permanents. See rule 702.131, “Ascend.”

documents.title: Clash
documents.text: To have a mini-contest involving the top cards of players’ libraries. See rule 701.30, “Clash.”

documents.title: Class
documents.text: An enchantment subtype. Classes have a number of class level abilities that increase their level and grant them new abilities. See rule 716, “Class Cards.”

documents.title: Cleanup Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the second and final step of the ending phase. See rule 514, “Cleanup Step.”

documents.title: Cleave
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to pay an alternative cost to remove some of a spell’s text. See rule 702.148, “Cleave.”

documents.title: Cloak
documents.text: A keyword action that puts a card onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. See rule 701.58, “Cloak,” and rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”

documents.title: Clue Token
documents.text: A Clue token is a colorless artifact token with “{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Collect Evidence
documents.text: A keyword action. To “collect evidence N” means to exile any number of cards from your graveyard with total mana value N or greater. See rule 701.59, “Collect Evidence.”

documents.title: Collector Number
documents.text: A number printed on most cards that has no effect on game play. See rule 213, “Information Below the Text Box.”

documents.title: Color
documents.text:
1. A characteristic of an object. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”
2. An attribute mana may have. See rule 106, “Mana.”

documents.title: Color Identity
documents.text: A set of colors that determines what cards may be included in a deck for the Commander casual variant. See rule 903.4.

documents.title: Color Indicator
documents.text: A characteristic of an object. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 204, “Color Indicator.”

documents.title: Colorless
documents.text:
1. An object with no color is colorless. Colorless is not a color. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”
2. A type of mana. See rule 106, “Mana,” and rule 107.4c.

documents.title: Combat Damage
documents.text: Damage dealt during the combat damage step by attacking creatures and blocking creatures as a consequence of combat. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

documents.title: Combat Damage Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the fourth step of the combat phase. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

documents.title: Combat Phase
documents.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the third phase of the turn. See rule 506, “Combat Phase.”

documents.title: Command
documents.text: A zone for certain specialized objects that have an overarching effect on the game, yet are not permanents and cannot be destroyed. See rule 408, “Command.”

documents.title: Commander
documents.text:
1. A casual variant in which each deck is led by a legendary card (usually a creature). See rule 903, “Commander.”
2. A designation given to one legendary card in each player’s deck in the Commander casual variant.

documents.title: Commander Draft
documents.text: A casual variant in which players participate in a booster draft and then play multiplayer games. See rule 903.13, “Commander Draft.”

documents.title: Commander Ninjutsu
documents.text: A variant of the ninjutsu ability. See rule 702.49, “Ninjutsu.”

documents.title: Commander Tax
documents.text: Informal term for the additional cost to cast a commander based on the number of times a player has cast it previously this game. See rule 903.8.

documents.title: Companion
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a player to choose one creature card from outside the game as a companion if the restriction of that card’s companion ability is met. Once a player has chosen a companion, that player may pay {3} to put it into their hand once during the game. See rule 702.139, “Companion.”

documents.title: Compleated
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a planeswalker to enter the battlefield with fewer loyalty counters if a player chose to pay life for Phyrexian mana symbols in its cost. See rule 702.150, “Compleated.”

documents.title: Complete a Dungeon
documents.text: To remove a dungeon card from the game after reaching that dungeon card’s bottommost room. See rule 309, “Dungeons.”

documents.title: Concede
documents.text: To quit the game. Conceding a game immediately causes that player to leave that game and lose that game. See rule 104, “Ending the Game.”

documents.title: Connive
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a player to draw a card, discard a card, and then to put a +1/+1 counter on a creature if a nonland card was discarded this way. See rule 701.50, “Connive.”

documents.title: Conspiracy
documents.text: A card type used in Limited formats such as Conspiracy Draft. A conspiracy card is not a permanent. See rule 315, “Conspiracies.”

documents.title: Conspiracy Draft
documents.text: A casual variant in which players participate in a booster draft and then play multiplayer games. See rule 905, “Conspiracy Draft.”

documents.title: Conspire
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates a copy of a spell. See rule 702.78, “Conspire.”

documents.title: Constructed
documents.text: A way of playing in which each player creates their own deck ahead of time. See rule 100.2a.

documents.title: Continuous Artifact (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term that appeared on the type line of artifacts without activated abilities. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to simply say “Artifact.”

documents.title: Continuous Effect
documents.text: An effect that modifies characteristics of objects, modifies control of objects, or affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period. See rule 611, “Continuous Effects.”

documents.title: Control, Controller
documents.text: “Control” is the system that determines who gets to use an object in the game. An object’s “controller” is the player who currently controls it. See rule 108.4.

documents.title: Control Another Player
documents.text: To make all choices and decisions that player is allowed to make, or is told to make, by rules or by any objects. See rule 723, “Controlling Another Player.”

documents.title: Convert
documents.text: To turn a double-faced card so its other face is up. See rule 701.28, “Convert.”

documents.title: Converted Mana Cost (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for mana value. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Convoke
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you tap creatures rather than pay mana to cast a spell. See rule 702.51, “Convoke.”

documents.title: Copiable Values
documents.text: Values of an object’s characteristics that are checked by copy effects. See rules 613.2, 707.2, and 707.3.

documents.title: Copy
documents.text:
1. To create a new object whose copiable values have been set to those of another object.
2. An object whose copiable values have been set to those of another object.
See rule 707, “Copying Objects.”

documents.title: Cost
documents.text: An action or payment necessary to take another action or to stop another action from taking place. See rule 118, “Costs.”

documents.title: Counter
documents.text:
1. To cancel a spell or ability so it doesn’t resolve and none of its effects occur. See rule 701.6, “Counter.”
2. A marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics or interacts with a rule or ability. See rule 122, “Counters.”

documents.title: Counts As (Obsolete)
documents.text: Some older cards were printed with text stating that the card “counts as” something. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to state that the card actually is that thing.

documents.title: Craft
documents.text: Craft is an activated ability that allows a player to exile cards from their graveyard and/or permanents they control to exile the permanent with the craft ability and return it onto the battlefield transformed. See rule 702.167, “Craft.”

documents.title: Create
documents.text: To create a token is to put a token onto the battlefield. See rule 701.7, “Create.”

documents.title: Creature
documents.text: A card type. A creature is a permanent. See rule 302, “Creatures.”

documents.title: Creature Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the creature card type and the kindred card type. See rule 302, “Creatures,” and rule 308, “Kindreds.” See rule 205.3m for the list of creature types.

documents.title: Crew
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you tap creatures to turn a Vehicle into an artifact creature. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.122, “Crew.”

documents.title: Crime
documents.text: Targeting an opponent, anything that opponent controls, and/or any cards in an opponent’s graveyard is a crime. See rule 700.13.

documents.title: Cumulative Upkeep
documents.text: A keyword ability that imposes an increasing cost to keep a permanent on the battlefield. See rule 702.24, “Cumulative Upkeep.”

documents.title: Cycling
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a card be discarded and replaced with a new card. See rule 702.29, “Cycling.”

documents.title: Damage
documents.text: Objects can deal “damage” to creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the object or player that receives that damage. See rule 120, “Damage.”

documents.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
documents.text: Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

documents.title: Dash
documents.text: A keyword ability found on creature cards that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule 702.109, “Dash.”

documents.title: Day
documents.text: Along with night, a designation the game can have. See rule 731, “Day and Night,” and rule 702.145, “Daybound and Nightbound.”

documents.title: Daybound
documents.text: An ability found on the front faces of some double-faced cards. Cards with daybound and nightbound are face up when it’s day and face down when it’s night. See rule 702.145, “Daybound and Nightbound,” and rule 731, “Day and Night.”

documents.title: Deal
documents.text: See Damage.

documents.title: Deathtouch
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes damage dealt by an object to be especially effective. See rule 702.2, “Deathtouch.”

documents.title: Decayed
documents.text: A keyword ability that means “This creature can’t block” and “When this creature attacks, sacrifice it at end of combat. See rule 702.147, “Decayed.”

documents.title: Deck
documents.text: The collection of cards a player starts the game with; it becomes that player’s library. See rule 100, “General,” and rule 103, “Starting the Game.”

documents.title: Declare Attackers
documents.text: To choose a set of creatures that will attack, declare whether each creature is attacking the defending player or a planeswalker that player controls, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to attack. See rule 508.1.

documents.title: Declare Attackers Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the second step of the combat phase. See rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

documents.title: Declare Blockers
documents.text: To choose a set of creatures that will block, declare which attacking creature each creature is blocking, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to block. See rule 509.1.

documents.title: Declare Blockers Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the third step of the combat phase. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

documents.title: Defender
documents.text: A keyword ability that prohibits a creature from attacking. See rule 702.3, “Defender.”

documents.title: Defending Player
documents.text: The player who can be attacked, and whose planeswalkers can be attacked, during the combat phase. See rule 506.2. In certain multiplayer games, there may be more than one defending player; see rule 802, “Attack Multiple Players Option,” and rule 805.10.

documents.title: Defending Team
documents.text: The team who can be attacked, and whose planeswalkers can be attacked, during the combat phase of a multiplayer game using the shared team turns option. See rule 805, “Shared Team Turns Option.”

documents.title: Defense
documents.text:
1. Part of a card that only battle cards have. A battle card’s defense is printed in its lower right corner. See rule 210, “Defense.”
2. A characteristic that only battles can have. See rule 310, “Battles.”

documents.title: Delayed Triggered Ability
documents.text: An ability created by effects generated when some spells or abilities resolve, or when some replacement effects are applied, that does something later on rather than at that time. See rule 603.7.

documents.title: Delve
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you exile cards from your graveyard rather than pay generic mana to cast a spell. See rule 702.66, “Delve.”

documents.title: Demonstrate
documents.text: A triggered ability found on some spells that let its controller copy it and choose an opponent to also copy it. See rule 702.144, “Demonstrate.”

documents.title: Dependency
documents.text: A system that may be used to determine in which order continuous effects in the same layer or sublayer are applied. See rule 613.8. See also Timestamp Order.

documents.title: Deploy Creatures Option
documents.text: An option that may be used in certain multiplayer variants to pass control of creatures between teammates. See rule 804, “Deploy Creatures Option.”

documents.title: Destroy
documents.text: To move a permanent from the battlefield to its owner’s graveyard. See rule 701.8, “Destroy.”

documents.title: Detain
documents.text: A keyword action that temporarily stops a permanent from attacking, blocking, or having its activated abilities activated. See rule 701.35, “Detain.”

documents.title: Dethrone
documents.text: A keyword ability that puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature when it attacks the player with the most life. See rule 702.105, “Dethrone.”

documents.title: Devoid
documents.text: A characteristic-defining ability that makes an object colorless. See rule 702.114, “Devoid.”

documents.title: Devotion
documents.text: A numerical value a player has, equal to the number of mana symbols of a certain color among the mana costs of permanents that player controls. See rule 700.5.

documents.title: Devour
documents.text: A keyword ability that can have a creature enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 702.82, “Devour.”

documents.title: Dies
documents.text: A creature or planeswalker “dies” if it is put into a graveyard from the battlefield. See rule 700.4.

documents.title: Discard
documents.text: To move a card from its owner’s hand to that player’s graveyard. See rule 701.9, “Discard.”

documents.title: Discover
documents.text: A keyword ability that may allow a player to cast a random spell for free. See rule 701.57, “Discover.”

documents.title: Disguise
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a card be cast face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. See rule 702.168, “Disguise,” and rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”

documents.title: Disturb
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a player to cast a double-faced card transformed from the graveyard. See rule 702.146, “Disturb.”

documents.title: Doctor’s Companion
documents.text: A partner ability that allows a player to play with two legendary creature cards as their commander if one of them has Doctor’s companion and the other is a Time Lord Doctor with no other creature types.

documents.title: Door
documents.text: A door is one half of a Room permanent. See rule 709, “Split Cards.”

documents.title: Double
documents.text: A keyword action used in a variety of contexts. See rule 701.10, “Double.”

documents.title: Double Agenda
documents.text: A variant of the hidden agenda ability. See rule 702.106, “Hidden Agenda.”

documents.title: Double Strike
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage twice. See rule 702.4, “Double Strike.”

documents.title: Double-Faced Cards
documents.text: Cards with two faces, one on each side of the card, and no Magic card back. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

documents.title: Draft
documents.text:
1. A Limited format in which players choose cards one at a time from booster packs, then construct a deck solely from the chosen cards and basic land cards.
2. To choose a card during a draft and put it into your card pool.

documents.title: Draft Round
documents.text: Part of a draft in which each player opens an unopened booster pack and the cards in those booster packs are drafted. See rules 905.1a and 905.1b.

documents.title: Draw
documents.text:
1. To put the top card of a player’s library into their hand as a turn-based action or as the result of an effect that uses the word “draw.” See rule 121, “Drawing a Card.”
2. The result of a game in which neither player wins or loses. See rule 104.4.

documents.title: Draw Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the third and final step of the beginning phase. See rule 504, “Draw Step.”

documents.title: Dredge
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player return a card from their graveyard to their hand. See rule 702.52, “Dredge.”

documents.title: Dungeon
documents.text: A card type found on nontraditional Magic cards. A dungeon card is not a permanent. See rule 309, “Dungeons.”

documents.title: During (Obsolete)
documents.text: Some older cards used the phrase “during [phase], [action].” These abilities were called “phase abilities.” In general, cards that were printed with phase abilities have received errata in the Oracle card reference so they have abilities that trigger at the beginning of a step or phase. “During” still appears in current card text, but only in its normal English sense and not as game terminology.

documents.title: Earthbend
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a land to become a 0/0 creature with haste in addition to its other types and puts a number of +1/+1 counters on it. When that land dies or is put into exile, return it to the battlefield tapped under your control. See 701.66, “Earthbend.”

documents.title: Echo
documents.text: A keyword ability that imposes a cost to keep a permanent on the battlefield. See rule 702.30, “Echo.”

documents.title: EDH (Obsolete)
documents.text: An older name for the Commander casual variant. See rule 903, “Commander.”

documents.title: Effect
documents.text: Something that happens in the game as a result of a spell or ability. See rule 609, “Effects.”

documents.title: Embalm
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player exile a creature card from their graveyard to create a mummified token version of that card. See rule 702.128, “Embalm.”

documents.title: Emblem
documents.text: An emblem is a marker used to represent an object that has one or more abilities, but no other characteristics. See rule 114, “Emblems.”

documents.title: Emerge
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a spell for less by sacrificing a creature. See rule 702.119, “Emerge.”

documents.title: Emperor
documents.text: The middle player on each team in an Emperor game. See rule 809, “Emperor Variant.”

documents.title: Emperor Variant
documents.text: A multiplayer variant played among three-player teams. See rule 809, “Emperor Variant.”

documents.title: Empower Jace
documents.text: A keyword action that gives you a Jace planeswalker token and/or puts loyalty counters on a Jace token you already have. See rule 701.71, “Empower Jace.”

documents.title: Enchant
documents.text: A keyword ability that defines what an Aura spell can target and what an Aura permanent can be attached to. See rule 303, “Enchantments,” and rule 702.5, “Enchant.”

documents.title: Enchantment
documents.text: A card type. An enchantment is a permanent. See rule 303, “Enchantments.” See also Aura.

documents.title: Enchantment Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the enchantment card type. See rule 303, “Enchantments.” See rule 205.3h for the list of enchantment types.

documents.title: Encoded
documents.text: A term that describes the relationship between a permanent and a card exiled by a cipher ability. See rule 702.99, “Cipher.”

documents.title: Encore
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player exile a creature card from their graveyard to, for each opponent, create a token that’s a copy of that card to attack that opponent. See rule 702.141, “Encore”

documents.title: Encounter
documents.text: To move a phenomenon card off the top of a planar deck and turn it face up. See rule 312, “Phenomena.”

documents.title: End of Combat Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the fifth and final step of the combat phase. See rule 511, “End of Combat Step.”

documents.title: End Step
documents.text: Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the ending phase. See rule 513, “End Step.”

documents.title: End the Combat Phase
documents.text: To “end the combat phase” as the result of an effect is to perform an expedited process that skips everything else that would happen that phase. See rule 724, “Ending Turns and Phases.”

documents.title: End the Turn
documents.text: To “end the turn” as the result of an effect is to perform an expedited process that skips nearly everything else that would happen that turn. See rule 724, “Ending Turns and Phases.”

documents.title: Ending Phase
documents.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the fifth and final phase of the turn. See rule 512, “Ending Phase.”

documents.title: Endure
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you choose put +1/+1 counters on a creature or create a Spirit creature token. See rule 702.62, “Endure.”

documents.title: Enduring Story
documents.text: A designation a player can have. The storied keyword causes a player to get this designation once they control three permanents that are artifacts, Sagas, and/or legendary. See rule 702.195, “Storied.”

documents.title: Energy Symbol
documents.text: The energy symbol {E} represents one energy counter. To pay {E}, a player removes one energy counter from themselves.

documents.title: Enlist
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a creature that could have attacked to support another creature. See rule 702.154, “Enlist.”

documents.title: Enter
documents.text: In rules text, to enter the battlefield. See “Enters the Battlefield.”

documents.title: Enters the Battlefield
documents.text: A nontoken permanent enters the battlefield when it’s moved onto the battlefield from another zone. A token enters the battlefield as it’s created. See rules 403.3, 603.6a, 603.6d, and 614.12. This phrase has been shortened to simply “enters” in rules text on cards in most contexts.

documents.title: Entwine
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player choose all modes for a spell rather than just the number specified. See rule 702.42, “Entwine.”

documents.title: Epic
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player copy a spell at the beginning of each of their upkeeps at the expense of casting any other spells for the rest of the game. See rule 702.50, “Epic.”

documents.title: Equip
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player attach an Equipment to a creature they control. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.6, “Equip.”

documents.title: Equipment
documents.text: An artifact subtype. Equipment can be attached to creatures. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.6, “Equip.”

documents.title: Escalate
documents.text: A keyword ability on some modal spells that adds a cost for choosing additional modes. See rule 702.120, “Escalate.”

documents.title: Escape
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card from their graveyard. See rule 702.138, “Escape.”

documents.title: Eternalize
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player exile a creature card from their graveyard to create an eternalized token version of that card. See rule 702.129, “Eternalize.”

documents.title: Evasion Ability
documents.text: An ability that restricts what creatures can block an attacking creature. See rules 509.1b–c.

documents.title: Event
documents.text: Anything that happens in a game. See rule 700.1.

documents.title: Evoke
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a permanent to be sacrificed when it enters the battlefield. See rule 702.74, “Evoke.”

documents.title: Evolve
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you put a +1/+1 counter on a creature when a larger creature enters the battlefield under your control. See rule 702.100, “Evolve.”

documents.title: Exalted
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature better in combat. See rule 702.83, “Exalted.”

documents.title: Excess Damage
documents.text: Damage dealt to a creature greater than what would be lethal damage or damage dealt to a planeswalker greater than its loyalty. See rule 120.4a.

documents.title: Exchange
documents.text: To swap two things, such as objects, sets of objects, or life totals. See rule 701.12, “Exchange.”

documents.title: Exert
documents.text: A keyword action that stops a permanent from untapping during the next untap step of the player who exerted it. See rule 701.43, “Exert.”

documents.title: Exhaust
documents.text: An activated ability that may be activated only once. See rule 702.177, “Exhaust.”

documents.title: Exile
documents.text:
1. A zone. Exile is essentially a holding area for cards. It used to be known as the “removed-from-the-game” zone.
2. To put an object into the exile zone from whatever zone it’s currently in. An “exiled” card is one that’s been put into the exile zone.
See rule 406, “Exile.”

documents.title: Expansion Symbol
documents.text: A card’s expansion symbol is a small icon normally printed below the right edge of the illustration that has no effect on game play. See rule 206, “Expansion Symbol.”

documents.title: Expend
documents.text: A word found on some abilities that care how much mana a player has spent to cast spells this turn. See rule 700.14.

documents.title: Exploit
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you sacrifice a creature for a benefit. See rule 702.110, “Exploit.”

documents.title: Explore
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a player to reveal the top card of their library and then to take different actions depending on whether a land card is revealed this way. See rule 701.44, “Explore.”

documents.title: Extort
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you gain life and have opponents lose life whenever you cast a spell. See rule 702.101, “Extort.”

documents.title: Extra Turn
documents.text: A turn created by an effect of a spell or ability. See rule 500.7. For rules about extra turns in a multiplayer game using the shared team turns option, see 805.8. For rules about extra turns in a Grand Melee game, see rule 807.4.

documents.title: Fabricate
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you choose whether to create Servo tokens or put +1/+1 counters on a creature. See rule 702.123, “Fabricate.”

documents.title: Face a Villainous Choice
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a player to choose one of two listed choices. See rule 701.55, “Face a Villainous Choice.”

documents.title: Face Down
documents.text:
1. A card is “face down” if it’s physically positioned so the card back is showing. Cards in some zones are normally kept face down. See section 4, “Zones.”
2. A status a permanent may have. See rule 110.5 and rule 702.37, “Morph.”
3. Face-down spells have additional rules. See rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents,” and rule 702.37, “Morph.”

documents.title: Face Up
documents.text:
1. A card is “face up” if it’s physically positioned so the card front is showing. Cards in some zones are normally kept face up. See section 4, “Zones.”
2. A default status a permanent may have. See rule 110.5 and rule 702.37, “Morph.”

documents.title: Fading
documents.text: A keyword ability that limits how long a permanent remains on the battlefield. See rule 702.32, “Fading.”

documents.title: Fateseal
documents.text: To manipulate some of the cards on top of an opponent’s library. See rule 701.29, “Fateseal.”

documents.title: Fear
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.36, “Fear.”

documents.title: Fight
documents.text: When two creatures fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 701.14, “Fight.”

documents.title: Finality Counter
documents.text: A counter that exiles the permanent it is on if that permanent would go to the graveyard from the battlefield. See rule 122.1h.

documents.title: Firebending
documents.text: A keyword ability that adds red mana until end of combat whenever a creature with that ability attacks. See rule 702.189, “Firebending.”

documents.title: First Strike
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage before other creatures. See rule 702.7, “First Strike.”

documents.title: Flanking
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature better in combat. See rule 702.25, “Flanking.”

documents.title: Flash
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player play a card any time they could cast an instant. See rule 702.8, “Flash.”

documents.title: Flashback
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card from their graveyard. See rule 702.34, “Flashback.”

documents.title: Flavor Text
documents.text: Text in italics (but not in parentheses) in the text box of a card that has no effect on play. See rule 207.2.

documents.title: Flavor Word
