documents.text: An italicized word with no rules meaning that provides a flavorful description of an ability. See rule 207.2d.

documents.title: Flip Cards
documents.text: Cards with a two-part card frame (one part of which is printed upside down) on a single card. See rule 710, “Flip Cards.”

documents.title: Flipped
documents.text: A status a permanent may have. See rule 110.5 and rule 710, “Flip Cards.” See also Unflipped.

documents.title: Flipping a Coin
documents.text: A method of randomization with two possible outcomes of equal likelihood. See rule 705, “Flipping a Coin.”

documents.title: Flying
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.9, “Flying.”

documents.title: Food Token
documents.text: A Food token is a colorless artifact token with “{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: For Mirrodin!
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates a 2/2 red Rebel creature token and then attaches the Equipment with the ability to that token. See rule 702.163, “For Mirrodin!”

documents.title: Forage
documents.text: To pay a cost of exiling three cards from your graveyard or sacrificing a Food. See rule 701.61, “Forage.”

documents.title: Forecast
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows an activated ability to be activated from a player’s hand. See rule 702.57, “Forecast.”

documents.title: Forest
documents.text: One of the five basic land types. Any land with this subtype has the ability “{T}: Add {G}.” See rule 305.6.

documents.title: Forestcycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Forestwalk
documents.text: See Landwalk.

documents.title: Foretell
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player exile cards from their hand and cast them for an alternative cost on future turns. See rule 702.143, “Foretell.”

documents.title: Foretold
documents.text: A card exiled using the foretell special action becomes foretold. Other effects can also make an exiled card foretold. A spell was foretold if it was a foretold card in exile before it was cast.

documents.title: Fortification
documents.text: An artifact subtype. Fortifications can be attached to lands. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.67, “Fortify.”

documents.title: Fortify
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player attach a Fortification to a land they control. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.67, “Fortify.”

documents.title: Free-for-All
documents.text: A multiplayer variant in which a group of players compete as individuals against each other. See rule 806, “Free-for-All Variant.”

documents.title: Freerunning
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows certain spells to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule 702.173, “Freerunning.”

documents.title: Frenzy
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature better in combat. See rule 702.68, “Frenzy.”

documents.title: Full Party
documents.text: A player has a full party if the number of creatures in their party is four. See rule 700.8.

documents.title: Fuse
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a player to cast both halves of a split card. See rule 702.102, “Fuse.”

documents.title: Fused Split Spell
documents.text: A split card on the stack that has been cast using the fuse ability or a copy of such a card. See rule 702.102, “Fuse.”

documents.title: General
documents.text: Any player in the Emperor multiplayer variant who isn’t an emperor. See rule 809, “Emperor Variant.”

documents.title: Generic Mana
documents.text: Mana in a cost represented by numerical symbols (such as {1}) or variable symbols (such as {X}) that can be paid with mana of any type. See rule 107.4.

documents.title: Gift
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a spell’s caster to choose an opponent as to receive a benefit as the spell resolves or when the permanent with the ability enters. See rule 702.174, “Gift.”

documents.title: Global Enchantment (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for a non-Aura enchantment. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Goad
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a creature to be goaded until a player’s next turn. See rule 701.15, “Goad.”

documents.title: Goaded
documents.text: A designation a permanent can have. Goaded creatures are forced to attack and to attack a player other than the player that caused it to be goaded. See rule 701.15, “Goad.”

documents.title: Gold Token
documents.text: A Gold token is a colorless artifact token with “Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.” For more information on predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Graft
documents.text: A keyword ability that has a permanent enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it and can move those counters to other creatures. See rule 702.58, “Graft.”

documents.title: Grand Melee
documents.text: A multiplayer variant in which a large group of players (usually ten or more) compete as individuals against each other. See rule 807, “Grand Melee Variant.”

documents.title: Gravestorm
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates copies of a spell. See rule 702.69, “Gravestorm.”

documents.title: Graveyard
documents.text:
1. A zone. A player’s graveyard is their discard pile.
2. All the cards in a player’s graveyard.
See rule 404, “Graveyard.”

documents.title: Hand
documents.text:
1. A zone. A player’s hand is where that player holds cards they have drawn but not played yet.
2. All the cards in a player’s hand.
See rule 402, “Hand.”

documents.title: Hand Modifier
documents.text: A characteristic that only vanguards have. See rule 211, “Hand Modifier.”

documents.title: Harmonize
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card from their graveyard for a specific cost and lets them tap a creature they control to reduce that cost. See rule 702.180, “Harmonize.”

documents.title: Harness
documents.text: A keyword action that grants a permanent the harnessed designation. See rule 701.64, “Harness.”

documents.title: Harnessed
documents.text: A designation permanents can have. Infinity permanents have their ∞ abilities as long as they are harnessed. See rule 701.64, “Harness,” and rule 702.186, “∞ (Infinity).”

documents.title: Haste
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature ignore the “summoning sickness” rule. See rule 702.10, “Haste,” and rule 302.6.

documents.title: Haunt
documents.text: A keyword ability that exiles cards. A card exiled this way “haunts” a creature targeted by the haunt ability. See rule 702.55, “Haunt.”

documents.title: Heal
documents.text: To remove damage marked on a permanent. See rule 701.69, “Heal.”

documents.title: Heartwood Token
documents.text: A Heartwood token is a red and green artifact token with “{T}: Add {R} or {G}.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Hexproof
documents.text: A keyword ability that precludes a permanent or player from being targeted by an opponent. See rule 702.11, “Hexproof.”

documents.title: Hidden Agenda
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a conspiracy card to be put into the command zone face down. See rule 702.106, “Hidden Agenda.”

documents.title: Hidden Zone
documents.text: A zone in which not all players can be expected to see the cards’ faces. See rule 400.2. See also Public Zone.

documents.title: Hideaway
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player store a secret card. See rule 702.75, “Hideaway.”

documents.title: Historic
documents.text: An object is historic if it has the legendary supertype, the artifact card type, or the Saga subtype. See rule 700.6.

documents.title: Hone Counter
documents.text: A counter on an Equipment that gives the equipped creature +1/+0. See rule 122, “Counters.”

documents.title: Horsemanship
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.31, “Horsemanship.”

documents.title: Hybrid Card
documents.text: A card with one or more hybrid mana symbols in its mana cost. See rule 202.2f.

documents.title: Hybrid Mana Symbols
documents.text: A mana symbol that represents a cost that can be paid in one of two ways. See rule 107.4.

documents.title: Hybrid Phyrexian Mana Symbols
documents.text: A mana symbol that represents a cost that can be paid in one of three ways. See rule 107.4.

documents.title: Job Select
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates a 1/1 colorless Hero creature token and then attaches the Equipment with the ability to that token. See rule 702.182, “Job Select.”

documents.title: Junk Token
documents.text: A Junk token is a colorless artifact token with {T}, Sacrifice this token: Exile the top card of your library. You may play that card this turn. Activate only as a sorcery.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: If
documents.text: See Intervening “If” Clause.

documents.title: Illegal Action
documents.text: An action that violates the rules of the game and/or requirements or restrictions created by effects. See rule 733, “Handling Illegal Actions.”

documents.title: Illegal Target
documents.text: A target that no longer exists or no longer meets the specifications stated by the spell or ability that’s targeting it. See rule 608.2b.

documents.title: Illustration
documents.text: A picture printed on the upper half of a card that has no effect on game play. See rule 203, “Illustration.”

documents.title: Illustration Credit
documents.text: Information printed directly below the text box that has no effect on game play. See rule 213, “Information Below the Text Box.”

documents.title: Impending
documents.text: An ability on some creatures that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. If cast for its impending cost, it isn’t a creature for some period of time. See rule 702.176, “Impending.”

documents.title: Imprint
documents.text: “Imprint” used to be a keyword ability. It is now an ability word and has no rules meaning. All cards printed with the imprint keyword have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Improvise
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you tap artifacts rather than pay mana to cast a spell. See rule 702.126, “Improvise.”

documents.title: In Play (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for the battlefield. Cards that were printed with text that contain the phrases “in play,” “from play,” “into play,” or the like are referring to the battlefield and have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Battlefield.

documents.title: In Response To
documents.text: An instant spell that’s been cast, or an activated ability that’s been activated, while another spell or ability is on the stack has been cast or activated “in response to” the earlier spell or ability. See rule 117.7.

documents.title: Increment
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you put a +1/+1 counter on a creature whenever you cast a spell if the amount of mana you spent on it is greater than that creature’s power or toughness. See rule 702.191, “Increment.”

documents.title: Incubate
documents.text: A keyword action that creates an Incubator token with a specified number of +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 701.53, “Incubate.”

documents.title: Incubator Token
documents.text: An Incubator token is a double-faced token. Its front face is a colorless Incubator artifact with “{2}: Transform this token.” Its back face is a 0/0 colorless Phyrexian artifact creature named “Phyrexian Token.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Independent
documents.text: See Dependency.

documents.title: Indestructible
documents.text: A keyword ability that precludes a permanent from being destroyed. See rule 702.12.

documents.title: Infect
documents.text: A keyword ability that affects how an object deals damage to creatures and players. See rule 702.90, “Infect.”

documents.title: Infinity
documents.text:
1. An artifact subtype.
2. ∞ is a keyword found on Infinity cards that grants an ability as long as that permanent is harnessed. See rule 702.186, “∞ (Infinity),” and rule 701.64, “Harness.”

documents.title: Ingest
documents.text: A keyword ability that can exile the top card of a player’s library. See rule 702.115, “Ingest.”

documents.title: Initiative
documents.text: A designation a player can have. Some effects instruct a player to take the initiative. The player with the initiative ventures into Undercity whenever they take the initiative and at the beginning of their upkeep. See rule 726, “The Initiative.”

documents.title: Instant
documents.text: A card type. An instant is not a permanent. See rule 304, “Instants.”

documents.title: Instead
documents.text: Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects. The word “instead” indicates what an event will be replaced with. See rule 614, “Replacement Effects.”

documents.title: Interrupt (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete card type. All cards printed with this card type are now instants. All abilities that, as printed, said a player could “play as an interrupt” can now be activated like any other activated abilities (unless they’re mana abilities, in which case they follow those rules instead). All relevant cards have been given errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Intervening “If” Clause
documents.text: A specially worded condition checked as a triggered ability would trigger and again as it would resolve. See rule 603.4.

documents.title: Intimidate
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.13, “Intimidate.”

documents.title: Investigate
documents.text: A keyword action that creates a Clue artifact token. See rule 701.16, “Investigate.”

documents.title: Island
documents.text: One of the five basic land types. Any land with this subtype has the ability “{T}: Add {U}.” See rule 305.6.

documents.title: Islandcycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Islandhome (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete keyword ability that meant “This creature can’t attack unless defending player controls an Island” and “When you control no Islands, sacrifice this creature.” Cards printed with this ability have been given errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Islandwalk
documents.text: See Landwalk.

documents.title: Jump-Start
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card from their graveyard by discarding a card. See rule 702.133, “Jump-Start.”

documents.title: Keyword Ability
documents.text: A game term, such as “flying” or “haste,” used as shorthand for a longer ability or group of abilities. See rule 702, “Keyword Abilities.”

documents.title: Keyword Action
documents.text: A verb, such as “destroy” or “cast,” used as a game term rather than as its normal English meaning. See rule 701, “Keyword Actions.”

documents.title: Keyword Counter
documents.text: A marker placed on an object that modifies its characteristics by granting it a keyword. See rule 122, “Counters.”

documents.title: Kicker, Kicked
documents.text: Kicker is a keyword ability that represents an optional additional cost. A spell has been kicked if its controller declared the intention to pay any or all of its kicker costs. See rule 702.33, “Kicker.”

documents.title: Kindred
documents.text: A card type. Whether or not a kindred is a permanent depends on its other card type. See rule 308, “Kindreds.”

documents.title: Land
documents.text: A card type. A land is a permanent. See rule 305, “Lands.”

documents.title: Land Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the land card type. See rule 305, “Lands.” See rule 205.3i for the list of land types.

documents.title: Lander Token
documents.text: A Lander token is a colorless artifact token with “{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Landwalk
documents.text: A generic term for a group of keyword abilities that restrict whether a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.14, “Landwalk.”

documents.title: Last Known Information
documents.text: Information about an object that’s no longer in the zone it’s expected to be in, or information about a player who’s no longer in the game. This information captures that object’s last existence in that zone or that player’s last existence in the game. See rules 113.7a, 608.2b, 608.2h, and 800.4h.

documents.title: Layer
documents.text: A system used to determine in which order continuous effects are applied. See rule 613, “Interaction of Continuous Effects.” See also Dependency, Timestamp Order.

documents.title: Learn
documents.text: A keyword action that lets a player add a Lesson card to their hand from outside the game or discard a card to draw a card. See rule 701.48, “Learn.”

documents.title: Leaves the Battlefield
documents.text: A permanent “leaves the battlefield” when it’s moved from the battlefield to another zone, or (if it’s phased in) when it leaves the game because its owner leaves the game. See rules 603.6c and 603.10.

documents.title: Legal Text
documents.text: Information printed directly below the text box that has no effect on game play. See rule 213, “Information Below the Text Box.”

documents.title: Legend (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete creature type. Cards printed with this subtype have been given errata in the Oracle card reference so they have the legendary supertype instead. See Legendary.

documents.title: Legend Rule
documents.text: A state-based action that causes a player who controls two or more legendary permanents with the same name to put all but one into their owners’ graveyards. See rule 704.5j.

documents.title: Legendary
documents.text: A supertype that’s normally relevant on permanents. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.” See also Legend Rule.

documents.title: Lethal Damage
documents.text: An amount of damage greater than or equal to a creature’s toughness. See rules 120.4a, 120.6, 510.1, and 704.5g.

documents.title: Level
documents.text: A numerical designation a permanent may have. A Class enchantment’s level determines what other abilities it has. See rule 716, “Class Cards.”

documents.title: Level Symbol
documents.text: A symbol that represents a keyword ability indicating abilities, power, and toughness a leveler card may have. See rule 107.8 and rule 711, “Leveler Cards.”

documents.title: Level Up
documents.text: A keyword ability that can put level counters on a creature. See rule 702.87, “Level Up.” For class level abilities of Class cards, see rule 716, “Class Cards.”

documents.title: Leveler Cards
documents.text: Cards with striated text boxes and three power/toughness boxes. See rule 711, “Leveler Cards.”

documents.title: Library
documents.text:
1. A zone. A player’s library is where that player draws cards from.
2. All the cards in a player’s library.
See rule 401, “Library.”

documents.title: Life, Life Total
documents.text: Each player has an amount of “life,” represented by that player’s “life total.” Life may be gained or lost. See rule 119, “Life.”

documents.title: Life Modifier
documents.text: A characteristic that only vanguards have. See rule 212, “Life Modifier.”

documents.title: Lifelink
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a player to gain life. See rule 702.15, “Lifelink.”

documents.title: Limited
documents.text: A way of playing in which each player gets a quantity of unopened Magic product and creates their own deck on the spot. See rule 100.2.

documents.title: Limited Range of Influence
documents.text: An optional rule used in some multiplayer games that limits what a player can affect. See rule 801, “Limited Range of Influence Option.”

documents.title: Linked Abilities
documents.text: Two abilities printed on the same object such that one of them causes actions to be taken or objects to be affected and the other one directly refers to those actions or objects. See rule 607, “Linked Abilities.”

documents.title: Living Metal
documents.text: A keyword ability found on some Vehicles that turns them into a creature during your turn. See rule 702.161, “Living Metal.”

documents.title: Living Weapon
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates a 0/0 black Phyrexian Germ creature token and then attaches the Equipment with the ability to that token. See rule 702.92, “Living Weapon.”

documents.title: Local Enchantment (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for an Aura. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Lock
documents.text: To remove an unlocked designation from a permanent that has one or more unlocked halves. See rule 709.5g.

documents.title: Locked
documents.text: One half of a split permanent is “locked” if it doesn’t have the appropriate unlocked designation. See rule 709.5.

documents.title: London Mulligan
documents.text: Informal term for the current system of mulligan rules. See rule 103.5.

documents.title: Loop
documents.text: A set of actions that could be repeated indefinitely. See rule 732, “Taking Shortcuts.”

documents.title: Lose the Game
documents.text: There are several ways to lose the game. See rule 104, “Ending the Game,” rule 810.8 (for additional rules for Two-Headed Giant games), rule 809.5 (for additional rules for Emperor games), and rule 903.10 (for an additional rule for Commander games).

documents.title: Loyalty
documents.text:
1. Part of a card that only planeswalker cards have. A planeswalker card’s loyalty is printed in its lower right corner. See rule 209, “Loyalty.”
2. A characteristic that only planeswalkers have. See rule 306.5.

documents.title: Loyalty Ability
documents.text: An activated ability with a loyalty symbol in its cost. See rule 606, “Loyalty Abilities.”

documents.title: Madness
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card they discard. See rule 702.35, “Madness.”

documents.title: Main Game
documents.text: The game in which a spell (or ability) that created a subgame was cast (or activated). See rule 729, “Subgames.”

documents.title: Main Phase
documents.text: Part of the turn. The first, or precombat, main phase is the second phase of the turn. The second, or postcombat, main phase is the fourth phase of the turn. See rule 505, “Main Phase.”

documents.title: Mana
documents.text: The primary resource in the game. It is spent to pay costs, usually when casting spells and activating abilities. See rule 106, “Mana,” rule 107.4, and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”

documents.title: Mana Ability
documents.text: An activated or triggered ability that could create mana and doesn’t use the stack. See rule 605, “Mana Abilities.”

documents.title: Mana Burn (Obsolete)
documents.text: Older versions of the rules stated that unspent mana caused a player to lose life; this was called “mana burn.” That rule no longer exists.

documents.title: Mana Cost
documents.text: A characteristic, and part of a card. A card’s mana cost is indicated by the mana symbols printed in its upper right corner. See rule 107.4 and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”

documents.title: Mana Pool
documents.text: Where mana created by an effect is temporarily stored. See rule 106.4.

documents.title: Mana Source (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete card type. All cards printed with this card type are now instants. All abilities that, as printed, said a player could “play as a mana source” are now mana abilities. All relevant cards have been given errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Mana Symbol
documents.text: An icon that represents mana or a mana cost. See rule 107.4.

documents.title: Mana Value
documents.text: The total amount of mana in a mana cost, regardless of color. See rule 202.3.

documents.title: Manifest
documents.text: A keyword action that puts a card onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature. See rule 701.40, “Manifest,” and rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”

documents.title: Manifest Dread
documents.text: A keyword action that puts one of the top two cards of your library onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature. See rule 701.62, “Manifest Dread,” rule 701.40, “Manifest,” and rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”

documents.title: Map
documents.text: A Map token is a colorless Map artifact token with “{1}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: Target creature you control explores. Activate only as a sorcery.” See rule 701.44, “Explore.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Match
documents.text: A multiplayer game or a two-player series of games (usually best-two-of-three) played in a tournament. See rule 100.6.

documents.title: Max Speed
documents.text:
1. A player has max speed if their speed is 4. See rule 702.179, “Start Your Engines!”
2. A keyword ability that grants an ability to the permanent or card it’s on only if that permanent’s controller (or that card’s owner, if it isn’t on the battlefield) has a speed of 4. See rule 702.178, “Max Speed.”

documents.title: Maximum Hand Size
documents.text: The number of cards in hand a player must discard down to during their cleanup step. See rule 402.2 and 514.1.

documents.title: Mayhem
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to play cards you discarded this turn from your graveyard for an alternative cost. See rule 702.187, “Mayhem.”

documents.title: Megamorph
documents.text: A variant of the morph ability that puts a +1/+1 counter on the creature as it turns face up. See rule 702.37, “Morph.”

documents.title: Meld
documents.text: To turn two members of a meld pair so their back faces are up and combined into one oversized Magic card. See rule 701.42, “Meld.”

documents.title: Meld Cards
documents.text: Cards with a Magic card face on one side and half of an oversized Magic card face on the other. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

documents.title: Melee
documents.text: A keyword ability that improves an attacking creature based on the number of opponents you attacked. See rule 702.121, “Melee.”

documents.title: Menace
documents.text: An evasion ability that makes creatures unblockable by a single creature. See rule 702.111, “Menace.”

documents.title: Mentor
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets your bigger creatures power up your smaller creatures when they attack together. See rule 702.134, “Mentor.”

documents.title: Merged Permanent
documents.text: A card or token may merge with a permanent to form a merged permanent. This merged permanent is represented by more than one card and/or token. See rule 730, “Merging with Permanents.”

documents.title: Mill
documents.text: To mill a number of cards, a player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard. See rule 701.17.

documents.title: Minimum Deck Size
documents.text: If a rule or effect states that a player’s deck must contain at least a specific number of cards, that number is the player’s minimum deck size.

documents.title: Miracle
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you cast a spell for a reduced cost if it’s the first card you draw in a turn. See rule 702.94, “Miracle.”

documents.title: Mobilize
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates a number of tapped and attacking red Warrior creature tokens that are sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step. See rule 702.181, “Mobilize.”

documents.title: Modal, Mode
documents.text: A spell or ability is “modal” if it has two or more options in a bulleted list preceded by instructions for a player to choose a number of those options, such as “Choose one —.” See rule 700.2.

documents.title: Modal Double-Faced Cards
documents.text: One kind of double-faced card. Modal double-faced cards can be played with either of their two faces up. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

documents.title: Modified
documents.text: A modified creature is a creature that has a counter on it, is equipped, or is enchanted by an Aura its controller also controls. See rule 700.9.

documents.title: Modular
documents.text: A keyword ability that has a permanent enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters on it and can move those counters to other artifact creatures. See rule 702.43, “Modular.”

documents.title: Monarch
documents.text: A designation a player can have. Some effects instruct a player to become the monarch. The monarch draws a card at the beginning of their end step. Dealing combat damage to the monarch steals the title from that player. See rule 725, “The Monarch.”

documents.title: Mono Artifact (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term that appeared on the type line of artifacts with activated abilities that caused the artifact to become tapped as a cost. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to simply say “Artifact,” and those abilities now include the tap symbol in their costs.

documents.title: Monocolored
documents.text: An object with exactly one color is monocolored. Colorless objects aren’t monocolored. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”

documents.title: Monocolored Hybrid Mana Symbols
documents.text: See Hybrid Mana Symbols.

documents.title: Monstrosity
documents.text: A keyword action that puts +1/+1 counters on a creature and makes it become monstrous. See rule 701.37, “Monstrosity.”

documents.title: Monstrous
documents.text: A designation given to a creature whose ability including a monstrosity instruction has resolved. See rule 701.37, “Monstrosity.”

documents.title: More Than Meets the Eye
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows some cards to be cast converted. See rule 702.162, “More Than Meets the Eye,” and rule 701.28, “Convert.”

documents.title: Morph
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a card be cast face down as a 2/2 creature. See rule 702.37, “Morph,” and rule 708, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”

documents.title: Mountain
documents.text: One of the five basic land types. Any land with this subtype has the ability “{T}: Add {R}.” See rule 305.6.

documents.title: Mountaincycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Mountainwalk
documents.text: See Landwalk.

documents.title: Move
documents.text:
To remove a counter from one object and put it on a different object. See rule 122.5.
Some older cards used “move” with respect to Auras; those cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference and now use the word “attach.”

documents.title: Mulligan
documents.text: To take a mulligan is to reject a prospective opening hand in favor of a new one. See rule 103.5.

documents.title: Multicolored
documents.text: An object with two or more colors is multicolored. Multicolored is not a color. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”

documents.title: Multikicker
documents.text: Multikicker is a variant of the kicker keyword ability. It represents an optional additional cost that may be paid any number of times. See rule 702.33, “Kicker.” See also Kicker.

documents.title: Multiplayer Game
documents.text: A game that begins with more than two players. See section 8, “Multiplayer Rules.”

documents.title: Mutate
documents.text: A keyword that lets a creature card be cast as a mutating creature spell. See rule 702.140, “Mutate.”

documents.title: Mutating Creature Spell
documents.text: A creature spell cast using the mutate keyword ability. As it resolves, if its target creature is legal, it merges with the target creature. The resulting creature has all characteristics of the topmost component and has the abilities of each component. See rule 702.140, “Mutate,” and rule 730, “Merging with Permanents.”

documents.title: Myriad
documents.text: Myriad is a triggered ability that effectively lets a creature attack in all possible directions. See rule 702.116, “Myriad.”

documents.title: Name
documents.text: A characteristic, and part of a card. A card’s name is printed in its upper left corner. See rule 201, “Name.”

documents.title: Night
documents.text: Along with day, a designation the game can have. See rule 731, “Day and Night,” and rule 702.145, “Daybound and Nightbound.”

documents.title: Nightbound
documents.text: An ability found on the back faces of some double-faced cards. Cards with daybound and nightbound are face up when it’s day and face down when it’s night. See rule 702.145, “Daybound and Nightbound,” and rule 731, “Day and Night.”

documents.title: Ninjutsu
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature suddenly enter combat. See rule 702.49, “Ninjutsu.”

documents.title: Nonbasic Land
documents.text: Any land that doesn’t have the supertype “basic.” See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.”

documents.title: Nonmodal Double-Faced Card
documents.text: One kind of double-faced card. Nonmodal double-faced cards default to being cast with their front faces up but can transform to their back faces in some way. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

documents.title: Nontraditional Magic Card
documents.text: A card not included in players’ decks. It may be oversized or have a card back other than a “Deckmaster” back. See rule 108.2.

documents.title: Object
documents.text: An ability on the stack, a card, a copy of a card, an emblem, a token, a spell, or a permanent. See rule 109, “Objects.”

documents.title: Offering
documents.text: A keyword ability that modifies when you can cast a spell and how much mana you need to spend to do it. See rule 702.48, “Offering.”

documents.title: Offspring
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to pay an additional cost as you cast a creature spell to create a 1/1 token that’s a copy of that permanent when it enters the battlefield. See rule 702.175, “Offspring.”

documents.title: Omen Card
documents.text: Cards with a two-part card frame (one part of which is inset on the left) on a single card where the alternative characteristics include the Omen spell type. See rule 720, “Omen Cards.”

documents.title: One-Shot Effect
documents.text: An effect that does something just once and doesn’t have a duration. See rule 610, “One-Shot Effects.” See also Continuous Effects.

documents.title: Ongoing
documents.text: A supertype that appears only on scheme cards. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.”

documents.title: Opening Hand
documents.text: The hand of cards a player starts the game with, once the player has decided not to take any further mulligans. See rule 103.5.

documents.title: Opponent
documents.text: Someone a player is playing against. See rules 102.2 and 102.3.

documents.title: Option
documents.text: An additional rule or set of rules that can be used in a multiplayer game. See rule 800.2.

documents.title: Oracle
documents.text: The reference that contains the up-to-date wordings (in English) for all tournament-legal cards. A card’s Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com. See rule 108.1.

documents.title: Outlast
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a creature to grow larger over time. See rule 702.107, “Outlast.”

documents.title: Outside the Game
documents.text: An object is “outside the game” if it isn’t in any of the game’s zones. See rule 400.11.

documents.title: Overload
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a spell to affect either a single target or many objects. See rule 702.96, “Overload.”

documents.title: Owner
documents.text: The player who (for purposes of the game) a card, permanent, token, or spell belongs to. See rules 108.3, 110.2, 111.2, and 112.2.

documents.title: Paired
documents.text: A term that describes a creature that’s been affected by a soulbond ability. See rule 702.95, “Soulbond.”

documents.title: Paradigm
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to cast a copy of a spell at the beginning of each of your first main phases. See rule 702.192, “Paradigm.”

documents.title: Partner, “Partner—[text],” “Partner with [name]”
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets two legendary cards be your commander in the Commander variant rather than one. “Partner with [name]” is a specialized version of the ability that works even outside of the Commander variant to help two cards reach the battlefield together. See rule 702.124, “Partner,” and rule 903, “Commander.”

documents.title: Party
documents.text: Some cards refer to the number of creatures in your party. A player’s party includes up to one each of Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and Wizard. See rule 700.8.

documents.title: Pass
documents.text: To decline to take any action (such as casting a spell or activating an ability) when you have priority. See rule 117, “Timing and Priority.”

documents.title: Pass in Succession
documents.text: All players “pass in succession” if each player in the game (starting with any one of them) opts not to take an action upon receiving priority. See rule 117, “Timing and Priority.”

documents.title: Pawprint Symbol
documents.text: A symbol shaped like a pawprint that is used to indicate the modes on some modal spells. See rule 700.2i.

documents.title: Pay
documents.text: To perform the actions required by a cost. This often means, but is not restricted to, spending resources such as mana or life. See rule 118, “Costs.”

documents.title: Permanent
documents.text: A card or token on the battlefield. See rule 110, “Permanents.”

documents.title: Permanent Card
documents.text: A card that could be put onto the battlefield. See rule 110.4a.

documents.title: Permanent Spell
documents.text: A spell that will enter the battlefield as a permanent as part of its resolution. See rule 110.4b.

documents.title: Permanently (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term used to indicate that a continuous effect has no duration and thus lasts until the end of the game. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference to delete it.

documents.title: Persist
documents.text: A keyword ability that can return a creature from the graveyard to the battlefield. See rule 702.79, “Persist.”

documents.title: Phase
documents.text:
1. A subsection of a turn. See section 5, “Turn Structure.”
2. A permanent “phases in” when its status changes from phased out to phased in. A permanent “phases out” when its status changes from phased in to phased out. See rule 702.26, “Phasing.”

documents.title: Phased In, Phased Out
documents.text: A status a permanent may have. Phased-in is the default status. Phased-out permanents are treated as though they do not exist. See rule 110.5 and rule 702.26, “Phasing.” (“Phased-out” was a zone in older versions of the rules.)

documents.title: Phasing
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a permanent to sometimes be treated as though it does not exist. See rule 702.26, “Phasing.”

documents.title: Phenomenon
documents.text: A card type seen only on nontraditional Magic cards in the Planechase casual variant. A phenomenon card is not a permanent. See rule 312, “Phenomena.”

documents.title: Phyrexian Mana Symbol
documents.text: A mana symbol that represents a cost that can be paid either by spending colored mana or by paying life. See rule 107.4.

documents.title: Phyrexian Symbol
documents.text: A symbol used in rules text to represent any of the five Phyrexian mana symbols. See rule 107.4g.

documents.title: Pile
documents.text: A temporary grouping of cards. See rule 700.3.

documents.title: Placed
documents.text: (Obsolete) Some spells and abilities previously referred to a counter being “placed” on a permanent. These cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference to use the term “put” instead. Due to a rules change, these cards continue to function as they did before. See rule 122, “Counters.”

documents.title: Plains
documents.text: One of the five basic land types. Any land with this subtype has the ability “{T}: Add {W}.” See rule 305.6.

documents.title: Plainscycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Plainswalk
documents.text: See Landwalk.

documents.title: Planar Deck
documents.text: A deck of at least ten plane cards needed to play the Planechase casual variant. See rule 901.3.

documents.title: Planar Die
documents.text: A specialized six-sided die needed to play the Planechase casual variant. See rule 901.3.

documents.title: Plane
documents.text: A card type seen only on nontraditional Magic cards in the Planechase casual variant. A plane card is not a permanent. See rule 311, “Planes.”

documents.title: Planechase
documents.text: A casual variant in which plane cards and phenomenon cards add additional abilities and randomness to the game. See rule 901, “Planechase.”

documents.title: Planeswalk
documents.text: To put each face-up plane card or phenomenon card on the bottom of its owner’s planar deck face down, then move the top card of your planar deck off that planar deck and turn it face up in a Planechase game. See rule 701.31, “Planeswalk.”

documents.title: Planeswalker
documents.text: A card type. A planeswalker is a permanent. See rule 306, “Planeswalkers.”

documents.title: Planeswalker Symbol
documents.text: The Planeswalker symbol appears on the planar die in the Planechase casual variant. See rule 107.11.

documents.title: Planeswalker Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the planeswalker card type. See rule 306, “Planeswalkers.” See rule 205.3j for the list of planeswalker types.

documents.title: Planeswalker Uniqueness Rule (Obsolete)
documents.text: Older versions of the rules stated that a player who controlled two or more planeswalkers with the same planeswalker type would put all but one of those planeswalkers into their owners’ graveyards. This rule was called the “planeswalker uniqueness rule” and no longer exists.

documents.title: Play
documents.text:
1. To play a land is to put a land onto the battlefield as a special action. See rule 116, “Special Actions,” and rule 305, “Lands.”
2. To play a card is to play that card as a land or cast that card as a spell, whichever is appropriate. See rule 601, “Casting Spells.”
3. (Obsolete) Casting a spell used to be known as playing a spell. Cards with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Cast.
4. (Obsolete) Activating an activated ability used to be known as playing an activated ability. Cards with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Activate.
5. (Obsolete) The battlefield used to be known as the in-play zone. Cards that were printed with text that contains the phrases “in play,” “from play,” “into play,” or the like are referring to the battlefield and have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Battlefield.

documents.title: Player
documents.text: One of the people in the game. See rule 102, “Players.”

documents.title: Plot
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player exile cards from their hand and cast them without paying their mana cost on future turns. See rule 702.170, “Plot.”

documents.title: Plotted
documents.text: A card exiled using the plot special action becomes plotted. Other effects can also make an exiled card plotted. See rule 702.170, “Plot.”

documents.title: Poison Counter
documents.text: A counter that may be given to a player. See rule 122, “Counters,” and rule 704.5c.

documents.title: Poisoned
documents.text: Having one or more poison counters. See rule 122, “Counters.”

documents.title: Poisonous
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a player to get poison counters. See rule 702.70, “Poisonous.”

documents.title: Poly Artifact (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term that appeared on the type line of artifacts with activated abilities that didn’t cause the artifact to be tapped as a cost. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to simply say “Artifact.”

documents.title: Populate
documents.text: A keyword action that creates a copy of a creature token you control. See rule 701.36, “Populate.”

documents.title: Postcombat Main Phase
documents.text: A main phase that occurs after a combat phase. See Main Phase.

documents.title: Power
documents.text:
1. Part of a card that only creature cards have. A creature card’s power is printed before the slash in its lower right corner. See rule 208, “Power/Toughness.”
2. A characteristic that only creatures have. See rule 302.4.

documents.title: Powerstone Token
documents.text: A Powerstone token is a colorless artifact token with “{T}: Add {C}. This mana can’t be spent to cast a nonartifact spell.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Power-up
documents.text: A one-time activated ability found on permanents that costs less during the turn the permanent with the ability entered the battlefield. See rule 702.193, “Power-up.”

documents.title: Precombat Main Phase
documents.text: The first main phase of a turn. See Main Phase.

documents.title: Preparation Card
documents.text: Cards with a two-part card frame (one part of which is inset on the right) on a single card. See rule 722, “Preparation Cards.”

documents.title: Prepare Spell
documents.text: The inset frame of a preparation card that includes its alternative characteristics. See rule 722, “Preparation Cards.”

documents.title: Prepared
documents.text: A designation a permanent may have that allows you to cast a copy of that card with its alternative characteristics. See rule 722, “Preparation Cards.”

documents.title: Prevent
documents.text: A word used by prevention effects to indicate what damage will not be dealt. See rule 615, “Prevention Effects.”

documents.title: Prevention Effect
documents.text: A kind of continuous effect that watches for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevents the damage that would be dealt. See rule 615, “Prevention Effects.”

documents.title: Priority
documents.text: Which player can take actions at any given time is determined by a system of “priority.” See rule 117, “Timing and Priority.”

documents.title: Prize
documents.text: An additional reward for visiting some Attractions. See rule 702.159, “Visit.”

documents.title: Proliferate
documents.text: To give an additional counter to any number of players and/or permanents of each kind they already have. See rule 701.34, “Proliferate.”

documents.title: Protect, Protector
documents.text: Each battle has a player designated as its protector, and that player protects that battle. See rule 310.9.

documents.title: Protection
documents.text: A keyword ability that provides a range of benefits against objects with a specific quality. See rule 702.16, “Protection.”

documents.title: Prototype
documents.text: An ability which allows a prototype card to be cast with a secondary set of characteristics. See rule 718, “Prototype Cards,” and rule 702.160, “Prototype.”

documents.title: Prototype Card
documents.text: Cards with a two-part card frame (one part of which is inset under the type line) on a single card. See rule 718, “Prototype Cards.”

documents.title: Provoke
documents.text: A keyword ability that can force a creature to block. See rule 702.39, “Provoke.”

documents.title: Prowess
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a creature to get +1/+1 whenever its controller casts a noncreature spell. See rule 702.108, “Prowess.”

documents.title: Prowl
documents.text: A keyword ability that may allow a spell to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule 702.76, “Prowl.”

documents.title: Public Zone
documents.text: A zone in which all players can be expected to see the cards’ faces. See rule 400.2. See also Hidden Zone.

documents.title: Rad Counter
documents.text: A type of counter a player can have that causes that player to mill cards at the beginning of their precombat main phase, then lose 1 life and remove one rad counter for each nonland card milled this way. See rule 122, “Counters,” and rule 728, “Rad Counters.”

documents.title: Rampage
documents.text: A keyword ability that can make a creature better in combat. See rule 702.23, “Rampage.”

documents.title: Range of Influence
documents.text: See Limited Range of Influence.

documents.title: Ravenous
documents.text: A keyword ability found on some creature cards with {X} in their mana cost. The creature enters the battlefield with X +1/+1 counters on it, and you draw a card if X is 5 or more. See rule 702.156, “Ravenous.”

documents.title: Reach
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a creature to block an attacking creature with flying. See rule 702.17, “Reach.” See also Flying.

documents.title: Read Ahead
documents.text: A keyword ability found on some Sagas that allows their controller to choose which chapter it starts on. See rule 702.155, “Read Ahead.”

documents.title: Rebound
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows an instant or sorcery spell to be cast a second time. See rule 702.88, “Rebound.”

documents.title: Reconfigure
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows an Equipment creature to temporarily stop being a creature and become attached to another creature. See rule 702.151, “Reconfigure.”

documents.title: Recover
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player return a card from their graveyard to their hand. See rule 702.59, “Recover.”

documents.title: Recruit
documents.text: A keyword action that lets a player draw a card, discard a card, and then create a creature token if a nonland card was discarded. See rule 701.70, “Recruit.”

documents.title: Redirect (Obsolete)
documents.text: Some older cards were printed with the term “redirect” to indicate a redirection effect. Such cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference so they explicitly state that damage that would be dealt to one object or player is dealt “instead” to another. See Redirection Effect.

documents.title: Redirection Effect
documents.text: A kind of replacement effect that causes damage that would be dealt to one creature, planeswalker, or player to be dealt instead to another creature, planeswalker, or player. See rule 614.9.

documents.title: Reflexive Triggered Ability
documents.text: An ability that triggers based on actions taken earlier during a spell or ability’s resolution. See rule 603.12.

documents.title: Regenerate
documents.text: To replace a permanent’s destruction with an alternate sequence of events. See rule 701.19, “Regenerate.”

documents.title: Reinforce
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player put +1/+1 counters on a creature. See rule 702.77, “Reinforce.”

documents.title: Reminder Text
documents.text: Parenthetical text in italics in the text box of a card that summarizes a rule that applies to that card, but is not actually rules text and has no effect on play. See rule 207.2.

documents.title: Remove from Combat
documents.text: Certain events can cause an attacking or blocking creature, or a planeswalker that’s being attacked, to be “removed from combat.” A permanent that’s removed from combat has no further involvement in that combat phase. See rule 506.4.

documents.key: Remove from the Game, Removed, Removed-from-the-Game Zone (Obsolete)
documents.title: Remove from the Game, Removed, Removed-from-the-Game Zone (Obsolete)
documents.text: “Remove [something] from the game” is an obsolete term for “exile [something].” “The removed card” is an obsolete term for “the exiled card.” The removed-from-the-game zone is an obsolete term for the exile zone. Cards with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Exile.

documents.title: Renown
documents.text: A keyword ability that makes a creature stronger after it deals combat damage to a player. See rule 702.112, “Renown.”

documents.title: Renowned
documents.text: A designation given to a permanent as a result of the renown ability. See rule 702.112, “Renown.”

documents.title: Replacement Effect
documents.text: A kind of continuous effect that watches for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replaces that event with a different event. See rule 614, “Replacement Effects.”

documents.title: Replicate
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates copies of a spell. See rule 702.56, “Replicate.”

documents.title: Requirement
documents.text: An effect that forces one or more creatures to attack or block. See rules 508.1d and 509.1c.

documents.title: Resolve
documents.text: When the spell or ability on top of the stack “resolves,” its instructions are followed and it has its effect. See rule 608, “Resolving Spells and Abilities.”

documents.title: Respond
documents.text: To cast an instant spell or activate an ability while another spell or ability is already on the stack. See rule 117.7.

documents.title: Restart the Game
documents.text: To immediately end the current game and restart it. See rule 727, “Restarting the Game.”

documents.title: Restriction
documents.text: An effect that precludes one or more creatures from attacking or blocking. See rules 508.1c and 509.1b.

documents.title: Retrace
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player cast a card from their graveyard. See rule 702.81, “Retrace.”

documents.title: Reveal
documents.text: To show a card to all players for a brief time. See rule 701.20, “Reveal.”

documents.title: The Ring
documents.text: An emblem that may be created at the time the Ring tempts you. See rule 701.54, “The Ring Tempts You.”

documents.title: The Ring Tempts You
documents.text: A keyword action that causes a player to choose a creature they control to be their legendary Ring-bearer and may cause them to create an emblem called The Ring. See rule 701.54, “The Ring Tempts You.”

documents.title: Ring-bearer
documents.text: A designation that a creature can be given as the Ring tempts you. See rule 701.54, “The Ring Tempts You.”

documents.title: Riot
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player choose whether certain creatures enter the battlefield with haste or with a +1/+1 counter. See rule 702.136, “Riot.”

documents.title: Ripple
documents.text: A keyword ability that may let a player cast extra cards from their library for no cost. See rule 702.60, “Ripple.”

documents.title: Role
documents.text: Roles are colorless enchantment tokens. Each one has the Aura and Role subtypes and the enchant creature ability. If a permanent has more than one Role attached to it controlled by the same player, each of those Roles except the one with the most recent timestamp is put into its owner’s graveyard. See rule 303.7 and rules 111.10j–r.

documents.title: Roll a d20
documents.text: To roll a twenty-sided die. Similarly, a d4 is a four-sided die, a d6 is a six-sided die, and so on. See rule 706, “Rolling a Die.”

documents.title: Room
documents.text:
1. A subsection of a dungeon card. See rule 309, “Dungeons.”
2. An enchantment subtype found on some split cards. See rule 709, “Split Cards.”

documents.title: Room Ability
documents.text: A triggered ability that triggers whenever a player moves their venture marker into a room of a dungeon card. See rule 309, “Dungeons.”

documents.title: Rules Text
documents.text: A characteristic that defines a card’s abilities. See rule 207.1.

documents.title: Sacrifice
documents.text: To move a permanent you control to its owner’s graveyard. See rule 701.21, “Sacrifice.”

documents.title: Saddle
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you tap creatures to make another creature “saddled” until end of turn. See rule 702.171, “Saddle.”

documents.title: Saddled
documents.text: A designation given to a creature whose saddle ability has resolved. See rule 702.171, “Saddle.”

documents.title: Saga
documents.text: An enchantment subtype. Sagas have a number of chapter abilities that take effect over a number of turns to tell a story. See rule 714, “Saga Cards.”

documents.title: Scavenge
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows you to exile a creature card from your graveyard to put +1/+1 counters on a creature. See rule 702.97, “Scavenge.”

documents.title: Scheme
documents.text: A card type seen only on nontraditional Magic cards in the Archenemy casual variant. A scheme card is not a permanent. See rule 314, “Schemes.”

documents.title: Scheme Deck
documents.text: A deck of at least twenty scheme cards needed to play the Archenemy casual variant. See rule 904.3.

documents.title: Scry
documents.text: To manipulate some of the cards on top of your library. See rule 701.22, “Scry.”

documents.title: Search
documents.text: To look at all cards in a stated zone and possibly find a card that matches a given description. See rule 701.23, “Search.”

documents.title: Secondary Title Bar
documents.text: A smaller name line with the Oracle reference name of a card which has an alternate name in its upper left corner. See rule 201.6.

documents.title: Set Aside (Obsolete)
documents.text: “Set [something] aside” is an obsolete term for “exile [something].” Cards with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Exile.

documents.title: Set in Motion
documents.text: To move a scheme card off the top of your scheme deck and turn it face up. See rule 701.32, “Set in Motion.”

documents.title: Shadow
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked and which creatures it can block. See rule 702.28, “Shadow.”

documents.title: Shard Token
documents.text: A Shard token is a colorless enchantment token with “{2}, Sacrifice this token: Scry 1, then draw a card.” For more information on predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Shared Life Total
documents.text: In the Two-Headed Giant multiplayer variant, each team has a “shared life total” rather than each player having an individual life total. See rule 810, “Two-Headed Giant Variant.”

documents.title: Shared Team Turns Option
documents.text: An option that may be used in certain multiplayer variants, such as Two-Headed Giant and Archenemy. See rule 805, “Shared Team Turns Option.”

documents.title: Shield Counter
documents.text: A counter that protects a permanent from being damaged or destroyed. See rule 122.1c.

documents.title: Shortcut
documents.text: A mutually understood way for the game to advance forward a number of game choices (either taking an action or passing priority) without players needing to explicitly identify each such choice. See rule 732, “Taking Shortcuts.”

documents.title: Shroud
documents.text: A keyword ability that precludes a permanent or player from being targeted. See rule 702.18, “Shroud.”

documents.title: Shuffle
documents.text: To randomize the cards in a deck (before a game) or library (during a game). See rule 103.3 and rule 701.24.

documents.title: Sideboard
documents.text: Extra cards that may be used to modify a deck between games of a match. See rules 100.4.

documents.title: Siege
documents.text: A battle subtype. Only an opponent of a Siege’s controller can be its protector. When the last defense counter is removed, its controller exiles the Siege, then they may cast it transformed without paying its mana cost. See rule 310.12.

documents.title: Silver-Bordered
documents.text: Cards in certain sets and certain promotional cards are printed with a silver border. Silver-bordered cards are intended for casual play and may have features and text that aren’t covered by these rules.

documents.title: Skip
documents.text: Effects that use the word “skip” are replacement effects. The word “skip” indicates what events, steps, phases, or turns will be replaced with nothing. See rule 614, “Replacement Effects.”

documents.title: Skulk
documents.text: A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.118, “Skulk.”

documents.title: Slivercycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Sneak
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows a spell to be cast for an alternative cost, including returning an unblocked attacking creature to its owner’s hand. Creatures cast this way enter tapped and attacking.

documents.title: Snow
documents.text: A supertype that’s normally relevant on permanents. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.”

documents.title: Snow Mana Symbol
documents.text: The snow mana symbol {S} represents a cost that can be paid with one mana produced by a snow source. It can also represent mana from a snow source that was spent to pay a cost. See rule 107.4h.

documents.title: Snow-Covered (Obsolete)
documents.text: Some older cards were printed with the term “snow-covered” in their rules text. Except when referencing card names, such cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference to reference the supertype “snow” instead. See Snow.

documents.title: Solved
documents.text:
1. A designation a Case may have, allowing its last ability to affect the game. See rule 719, “Case Cards.”
2. A keyword ability of Case cards that affects the game only if the Case has the solved designation. See rule 702.169, “Solved.”

documents.title: Sorcery
documents.text: A card type. A sorcery is not a permanent. See rule 307, “Sorceries.”

documents.title: Soulbond
documents.text: A keyword ability that makes creatures better by pairing them together. See rule 702.95, “Soulbond.”

documents.title: Soulshift
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player return a card from their graveyard to their hand. See rule 702.46, “Soulshift.”

documents.title: Source of an Ability
documents.text: The object that generated that ability. See rule 113.7.

documents.title: Source of Damage
documents.text: The object that dealt that damage. See rule 609.7.

documents.title: Source of Mana
documents.text: The spell that produced mana or the source of the ability that produced mana. See rule 106.3.

documents.title: Space Sculptor
documents.text: A keyword ability that splits creatures on the battlefield into sectors. See rule 702.158, “Space Sculptor.”

documents.title: Special Action
documents.text: An action a player may take that doesn’t use the stack. See rule 116, “Special Actions.”

documents.title: Spectacle
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows certain spells to be cast for an alternative cost if an opponent has lost life. See rule 702.137, “Spectacle.”

documents.title: Speed
documents.text: Speed is a value that a player can have. See rule 702.179, “Start Your Engines!”

documents.title: Spell
documents.text: A card on the stack. Also a copy (of either a card or another spell) on the stack. See rule 112, “Spells.”

documents.title: Spell Ability
documents.text: A kind of ability. Spell abilities are abilities that are followed as instructions while an instant or sorcery spell is resolving. See rule 113.3a.

documents.title: Spell Type
documents.text: A subtype that’s correlated to the instant card type and the sorcery card type. See rule 304, “Instants,” and rule 307, “Sorceries.” See rule 205.3k for the list of spell types.

documents.title: Splice
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player add a card’s rules text onto another spell. See rule 702.47, “Splice.”

documents.title: Split Cards
documents.text: Cards with two card faces on a single card. See rule 709, “Split Cards.”

documents.title: Split Second
documents.text: A keyword ability that makes it nearly impossible for a player to respond to a spell. See rule 702.61, “Split Second.”

documents.title: Spree
documents.text: An ability found on some modal spells that allows you to choose one or more modes and requires you to pay additional costs for those modes. See rule 702.172, “Spree.”

documents.title: Squad
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates copies of a creature when it enters the battlefield. See rule 702.157, “Squad.”

documents.title: Stack
documents.text: A zone. The stack is the zone in which spells, activated abilities, and triggered abilities wait to resolve. See rule 405, “Stack.”

documents.title: Start Your Engines!
documents.text: A keyword ability that gives a player a speed of 1 if they have no speed. Once a player has speed, their speed increases once on each of their turns when an opponent loses life. See rule 702.179, “Start Your Engines!”

documents.title: Starting Deck
documents.text: After a player has set aside their sideboard, their remaining deck becomes their starting deck. See rule 103.2a.

documents.title: Starting Hand Size
documents.text: The number of cards a player draws as a game begins. In most games, each player’s starting hand size is seven. See rule 103.5.

documents.title: Starting Life Total
documents.text: The amount of life a player has as a game begins. In most games, each player’s starting life total is 20. See rule 103.4.

documents.title: Starting Player
documents.text: The player chosen to take the first turn of a game. See rule 103.1.

documents.title: Starting Team
documents.text: The team chosen to take the first turn of a game using the shared team turns option. See rule 103.1.

documents.title: State Trigger
documents.text: A triggered ability that triggers when a game state is true rather than triggering when an event occurs. See rule 603.8.

documents.title: State-Based Actions
documents.text: Game actions that happen automatically whenever certain conditions are met. See rule 704, “State-Based Actions.”

documents.title: Static Ability
documents.text: A kind of ability. Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. See rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 604, “Handling Static Abilities.”

documents.title: Station
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets you tap creatures to add charge counters to station cards. See rule 702.184, “Station,” and rule 721, “Station Cards.”

documents.title: Station Cards
documents.text: Cards with striated text boxes, one or more station symbols, and the station ability. See rule 721, “Station Cards.”

documents.title: Status
documents.text: The physical state of a permanent. See rule 110.5.

documents.title: Step
documents.text: A subsection of a phase. See section 5, “Turn Structure.”

documents.title: Sticker
documents.text: A marker placed on an object that modifies its characteristics or interacts with a rule or effect. See rule 123, “Stickers.”

documents.title: Sticker Kicker
documents.text: A kicker variant that can add a sticker to the spell with the ability and give a player a ticket counter. See rule 702.33h.

documents.title: Sticker Sheet
documents.text: The collection of stickers found on an insert in Unfinity booster packs. See rule 123, “Stickers.”

documents.title: Storied
documents.text: A keyword causing a player to get the enduring story designation once they control three or more permanents that are artifacts, Sagas, and/or legendary. See rule 702.195, “Storied.”

documents.title: Storm
documents.text: A keyword ability that creates copies of a spell. See rule 702.40, “Storm.”

documents.title: Stun Counter
documents.text: A counter that stops a permanent from untapping. See rule 122.1d.

documents.title: Subgame
documents.text: A completely separate Magic game created by an effect. See rule 729, “Subgames.”

documents.title: Substitute Card
documents.text: A game supplement with a Magic card back that can be used to represent a double-faced card or meld card. See rule 713, “Substitute Cards.”

documents.title: Subtype
documents.text: A characteristic that appears after the card type and a long dash on a card’s type line. See rule 205.3, “Subtypes.”

documents.title: Successfully Cast (Obsolete)
documents.text: A term that was printed on some older cards. In general, cards that referred to a spell being “successfully cast” have received errata in the Oracle card reference to simply refer to a spell being “cast.”

documents.title: Summon (Obsolete)
documents.text: Older creature cards were printed with “Summon [creature type]” on their type lines. All such cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference to say “Creature — [creature type].” (Many of these cards’ creature types have also been updated.) See Creature.

documents.title: Summoning Sickness Rule
documents.text: Informal term for a player’s inability to attack with a creature or to activate its abilities that include the tap symbol or the untap symbol unless the creature has been under that player’s control since the beginning of that player’s most recent turn. See rule 302.6. See also Haste.

documents.title: Sunburst
documents.text: A keyword ability that can have a permanent enter the battlefield with +1/+1 counters or charge counters on it. See rule 702.44, “Sunburst.”

documents.title: Supertype
documents.text: A characteristic that appears before the card type on a card’s type line. Most cards don’t have a supertype. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.”

documents.title: Supervillain Rumble
documents.text: A Free-for-All game in which each player is an archenemy. See rule 806, “Free-for-All,” and rule 904, “Archenemy.”

documents.title: Support
documents.text: A keyword action that lets you put +1/+1 counters on creatures. See rule 701.41, “Support.”

documents.title: Surge
documents.text: A keyword ability that provides an alternative cost to cast a card if you or one of your teammates has cast another spell in the same turn. See rule 702.117, “Surge.”

documents.title: Surveil
documents.text: To manipulate some of the cards on top of your library, sending some of them to your graveyard and rearranging the rest. See rule 701.25, “Surveil.”

documents.title: Suspend
documents.text: A keyword ability that provides an alternative way to play a card. See rule 702.62, “Suspend.” A card is “suspended” if it’s in the exile zone, has suspend, and has a time counter on it.

documents.title: Swamp
documents.text: One of the five basic land types. Any land with this subtype has the ability “{T}: Add {B}.” See rule 305.6.

documents.title: Swampcycling
documents.text: See Typecycling.

documents.title: Swampwalk
documents.text: See Landwalk.

documents.title: Tap
documents.text: To turn a permanent sideways from an upright position. See rule 701.26, “Tap and Untap.”

documents.title: Tap Symbol
documents.text: The tap symbol {T} in an activation cost means “Tap this permanent.” See rule 107.5.

documents.title: Tapped
documents.text: A status a permanent may have. See rule 110.5 and rule 701.26, “Tap and Untap.” See also Untapped.

documents.title: Target
documents.text: A preselected object or player a spell or ability will affect. See rule 115, “Targets.”

documents.title: Team
documents.text: A group of players who share a common victory condition in a multiplayer game. See rule 808, “Team vs. Team Variant,” rule 809, “Emperor Variant,” rule 810, “Two-Headed Giant Variant,” and rule 811, “Alternating Teams Variant.”

documents.title: Team vs. Team Variant
documents.text: A multiplayer variant played among two or more teams, each of which sits together. See rule 808, “Team vs. Team Variant.”

documents.title: Teammate
documents.text: In a multiplayer game between teams, a player’s teammates are the other players on their team. See rule 102.3.

documents.title: Teamwork
documents.text: A keyword ability that represents an optional additional cost of tapping creatures. See rule 702.194, “Teamwork.”

documents.title: Text Box
documents.text: Part of a card. The text box is printed on the lower half of the card and contains the card’s rules text, reminder text, and flavor text. See rule 207, “Text Box.”

documents.title: Text-Changing Effect
documents.text: A continuous effect that changes the text that appears in an object’s text box and/or type line. See rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects.”

documents.title: Threshold
documents.text: “Threshold” used to be a keyword ability. It is now an ability word and has no rules meaning. All cards printed with the threshold keyword have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Ticket Symbol
documents.text: The ticket symbol {TK} with no numbers in it represents one ticket counter. The ticket symbol with a number in it represents a ticket cost. To pay a ticket cost, a player removes that many ticket counters from themselves.

documents.title: Tiered
documents.text: A keyword ability found on some modal spells that requires you to pay an additional cost for the mode you choose. See rule 702.183, “Tiered.”

documents.title: Time Travel
documents.text: To add a time counter to or remove a time counter from any number of permanents you control with a time counter on them or suspended cards you own in exile with time counters on them. See rule 701.56, “Time Travel.”

documents.title: Timestamp Order
documents.text: A system used to determine in which order continuous effects in the same layer or sublayer are applied. See rule 613.7. See also Dependency.

documents.title: Token
documents.text: A marker used to represent any permanent that isn’t represented by a card. See rule 111, “Tokens.”

documents.title: Tombstone Icon
documents.text: An icon that appears in the upper left of some Odyssey block cards that has no effect on game play. See rule 107.9.

documents.title: Total Casting Cost (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete term for mana value. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Total Cost
documents.text: What a player actually has to pay, in practical terms, to cast a spell or activated ability: the mana cost, activation cost, or alternative cost, plus all cost increases (including additional costs) and minus all cost reductions. See rule 601.2f.

documents.title: Totem Armor (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete keyword ability that has been renamed. See rule 702.89, “Umbra Armor.”

documents.title: Toughness
documents.text:
1. Part of a card that only creature cards have. A creature card’s toughness is printed after the slash in its lower right corner. See rule 208, “Power/Toughness.”
2. A characteristic that only creatures have. See rule 302.4.

documents.title: Tournament
documents.text: An organized play activity where players compete against other players. See rule 100.6.

documents.title: Tournament Rules
documents.text: Additional rules that apply to games played in a sanctioned tournament. See rule 100.6.

documents.title: Toxic
documents.text: A keyword ability that causes a player to get poison counters due to combat damage from creatures with the ability. See rule 702.164, “Toxic.”

documents.title: Traditional Magic Card
documents.text: A Magic card that measures approximately 2.5 inches (6.3 centimeters) by 3.5 inches (8.8 centimeters) and is included in players’ decks. See rule 108.2.

documents.title: Training
documents.text: A keyword ability that means “Whenever this creature and at least one other creature with power greater that this creature’s power attack, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.” See rule 702.149, “Training.”

documents.title: Trample
documents.text: A keyword ability that modifies how a creature assigns combat damage. See rule 702.19, “Trample.”

documents.title: Trample Over Planeswalkers
documents.text: A variant of trample that modifies how a creature assigns combat damage if it’s attacking a planeswalker. See rule 702.19, “Trample”

documents.title: Transfigure
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player search their library for a replacement creature card. See rule 702.71, “Transfigure.”

documents.title: Transform
documents.text: To turn a double-faced card so its other face is up. See rule 701.27, “Transform.”

documents.title: Transforming Double-Faced Cards (Obsolete)
documents.text: An older name for nonmodal double-faced cards. See rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards.”

documents.title: Transmute
documents.text: A keyword ability that lets a player search their library for a replacement card. See rule 702.53, “Transmute.”

documents.title: Treasure Token
documents.text: A Treasure token is a colorless artifact token with “{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

documents.title: Tribal (Obsolete)
documents.text: An obsolete card type that has been renamed. See rule 308, “Kindreds.”

documents.title: Tribute
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows an opponent to choose between a creature entering the battlefield with +1/+1 counters or an additional ability. See rule 702.104, “Tribute.”

documents.title: Trigger
documents.text: Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically “triggers.” That means its controller puts it on the stack the next time a player would receive priority. See rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

documents.title: Trigger Condition
documents.text: The first part of a triggered ability, consisting of “when,” “whenever,” or “at” followed by a trigger event. See rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

documents.title: Trigger Event
documents.text: The event that a triggered ability looks for. Whenever the trigger event occurs, the triggered ability triggers. See rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

documents.title: Triggered Ability
documents.text: A kind of ability. Triggered abilities begin with the word “when,” “whenever,” or “at.” They’re written as “[Trigger condition], [effect].” See rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

documents.title: Triple
documents.text: A keyword action that increases a creature’s power and/or toughness. See rule 701.11, “Triple.”

documents.title: Turn Markers
documents.text: Markers used to keep track of which players are taking turns in a Grand Melee game. See rule 807.4.

documents.title: Turn-Based Actions
documents.text: Game actions that happen automatically when certain steps or phases begin, or when each step or phase ends. See rule 703, “Turn-Based Actions.”

documents.title: Two-Headed Giant Variant
documents.text: A multiplayer variant played among two-player teams that each have a shared life total and take a simultaneous turn. See rule 810, “Two-Headed Giant Variant.”

documents.title: Type
documents.text:
1. An object’s card type or, more broadly, its card type, subtype, and/or supertype. See rule 205, “Type Line,” and section 3, “Card Types.”
2. An attribute mana has. See rule 106, “Mana.”

documents.title: Type Icon
documents.text: An icon that appears in the upper left of some Future Sight cards that has no effect on game play. See rule 107.10.

documents.title: Type Line
documents.text: Part of a card. The type line is printed directly below the illustration and contains the card’s card type(s), subtype(s), and/or supertype(s). See rule 205, “Type Line.”

documents.title: Type-Changing Effect
documents.text: An effect that changes an object’s card type, subtype, and/or supertype. See rules 205.1a–b, 305.7, and 613.1d.

documents.title: Typecycling
documents.text: A variant of the cycling ability. See rule 702.29, “Cycling.”

documents.title: Umbra Armor
documents.text: A keyword ability that allows an Aura to protect the permanent it’s enchanting. See rule 702.89, “Umbra Armor.”

documents.title: Unattach
documents.text: To move an Equipment away from the creature it’s attached to so that the Equipment is on the battlefield but is not equipping anything. See rule 701.3d.

documents.title: Unblockable (Obsolete)
documents.text: A term that meant “can’t be blocked.” Cards that used this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference.

documents.title: Unblocked Creature
documents.text: An attacking creature once no creature has been declared as a blocker for it, unless an effect has caused it to become blocked. It remains an unblocked creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

documents.title: Undaunted
